definition_zh: 班级；课；阶级；类别；等级
definition_en: a group of students taught together, a lesson, a social rank, or a group of things of the same type
core_image: 一间教室里按排坐好的学生，黑板写着课表
scene: 铃声响过，走廊一下空了，只有一间教室还亮着灯。She stayed behind after class to ask a question.
sceneCN: 这里 class 指「课」（第 1 个义项：按班级进行的一节课）；句意是下课后她留下来问了一个问题。

senses.title: A group of students or a lesson
senses.definition: a group of students taught together, or a period of teaching
senses.definitionCN: 一起上课的一群学生，或一节课
senses.example: Our class has thirty students this year.
senses.exampleCN: 我们班今年有三十名学生。
senses.why: The Latin word for a division of people was applied to the division of pupils in a school.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里表示人群划分的词，被用来指学校里学生的划分。

senses.title: A social rank
senses.definition: a group of people with a similar position in society
senses.definitionCN: 在社会中地位相近的一群人
senses.example: The novel follows a family across three social classes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说写一个家庭横跨三个社会阶层。
senses.why: Roman citizens were officially divided into ranks, and the word kept that meaning of a ranked group.
senses.whyCN: 罗马公民被正式分为不同等级，这个词保留了按等级分组的含义。

senses.title: A category of things
senses.definition: a group of things or people that share the same type or quality
senses.definitionCN: 属于同一类型或同一品质的一组事物或人
senses.example: This ticket is for a different class of seat.
senses.exampleCN: 这张票对应的是另一种等级的座位。
senses.why: Any division into groups can be called a class, so the word moved from people to objects.
senses.whyCN: 任何分组都可以叫 class，于是这个词从人扩展到了物。

intro.en: Class comes from the Latin name for a division of Roman citizens by property.
intro.cn: class 出自拉丁语，本指按财产对罗马公民所作的划分。

items.en: Classis divided Roman citizens into ranked groups.
items.cn: classis 把罗马公民按等级分组。

items.en: The word also named a fleet, that is, a group of ships.
items.cn: 这个词也指舰队，即一组船只。

items.en: Classe meant a group or an order of things.
items.cn: classe 指一群或一等级的事物。

items.en: English used class for school groups and for ranks of society.
items.cn: 英语用 class 指学校的班级与社会等级。

items.en: The word now covers any category, from hotel rooms to animals.
items.cn: 这个词如今涵盖任何类别，从酒店房型到动物分类。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words with a similar short shape, while the meaning group names kinds and levels.
note.cn: 形近组列出外形相近的短词，近义组列出种类与层级。

entries.definition: a hard clear material used in windows
entries.definitionCN: 用于窗户的坚硬透明材料

entries.definition: a part of a sentence with its own verb
entries.definitionCN: 带有自身动词的句子成分

entries.definition: stylish and of good quality
entries.definitionCN: 有格调且品质好的

entries.definition: a group of things of the same kind
entries.definitionCN: 同类事物构成的组

entries.definition: a level of quality or rank
entries.definitionCN: 品质或等级的层次

entries.definition: a period of teaching in a subject
entries.definitionCN: 某一科目的授课时段

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the school sense, the social sense and the sorting sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用学校义、社会阶层义与归类义。

normal.en: One word covers a school group, a social rank and a set of objects, because all three are divisions.
normal.cn: 一个词兼指学校班级、社会等级与一类物品，因为三者都是划分。

normal.en: After class and in class are fixed phrases with no article.
normal.cn: after class 与 in class 是固定说法，都不加冠词。

normal.en: The working class is a group of people, while first class is a level of service.
normal.cn: the working class 指一群人，first class 指一种服务等级。

normal.en: The plural classes adds a syllable, so it ends in a clear hiss.
normal.cn: 复数 classes 多一个音节，结尾有一声清晰的嘶音。

normal.en: Class is the noun, classify is the verb, and classification is the result.
normal.cn: class 是名词，classify 是动词，classification 是结果。

abstract.en: Picture rows of desks with a timetable pinned above the board.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排课桌，黑板上方钉着课表。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre with the cheap seats high up and the boxes below.
abstract.cn: 想象一座剧院，廉价座位在高处，包厢在下面。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer of screws sorted into small labelled boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象一抽屉螺钉被分进贴了标签的小盒里。

examples.en: Our class has thirty students this year.
examples.cn: 我们班今年有三十名学生。

examples.en: She stayed behind after class to ask a question.
examples.cn: 下课后她留下来问了一个问题。

examples.en: The novel follows a family across three social classes.
examples.cn: 这部小说写一个家庭横跨三个社会阶层。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「群」，ass 想成「一队」：一群人按等级排好，就成了班与阶级。

root: 源自拉丁语 classis（罗马公民的等级划分，也指舰队），经法语 classe 进入英语，由人群划分扩展为一切类别。

sensesIntro.en: A division of citizens becomes a school group, then a social rank, then any category.
sensesIntro.cn: 对公民的划分先变成学校班级，再变成社会等级，最后变成任何类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of pupils seated in a room under a timetable.
core.cn: 核心意象：教室里一排排坐好的学生，上方挂着课表。

branches.en: The ranked group becomes a group of pupils.
branches.cn: 按等级划分的群体变成了一个班的学生。

branches.en: Rank in society keeps the old Roman sense.
branches.cn: 社会等级保留了古罗马的含义。

branches.en: Any set of similar things can be one class.
branches.cn: 任何同类事物的集合都可以是一个类别。

branches.en: A school class is only one case of a general category.
branches.cn: 学校班级只是一般类别中的一个实例。

branches.en: Rank and kind both depend on sorting by a standard.
branches.cn: 等级与种类都依赖按某种标准分类。

intro.en: The noun takes a plural and a verb ending, and feeds a family of classifying words.
intro.cn: 这个名词接复数与动词词尾，并衍生出一组分类相关词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin classis, a division, which also gave classical and classify.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 classis（划分），classical 与 classify 也源于它。

items.meaning: a group, a lesson or a rank
more than one group or lesson
items.exampleCN: 两个班共用这间实验室。

items.example: The bird was classed as rare.
They are classing the finds by age.
items.exampleCN: 他们正按年代给这些发现物分类。

items.example: We classify the samples by size.
items.exampleCN: 我们按大小给样本分类。
这家酒店看起来很上档次。

items.meaning: a room where a class meets

latinEntries.example: Classis is the base of class and classify.
latinEntries.exampleCN: classis 是 class 与 classify 的词基。

definition_zh: 古典的；古希腊罗马的；古典音乐（传统）的；公认的
definition_en: belonging to ancient Greece and Rome, following a formal artistic tradition, or long established as standard
core_image: 石柱与三角山墙撑起的希腊神庙正面
scene: 音乐厅里调音完毕，观众安静下来。The orchestra opened with a piece of classical music from Vienna.
sceneCN: 这里 classical 指「古典音乐（传统）的」（第 2 个义项：属于欧洲严肃音乐的正式传统）；句意是乐团以一首维也纳古典乐曲开场。

pos.zh: 古典的；古希腊罗马的；古典音乐的

senses.title: Of ancient Greece and Rome
senses.definition: belonging to the civilisation of ancient Greece and Rome
senses.definitionCN: 属于古希腊与古罗马文明的
senses.example: He reads classical texts in the original.
senses.exampleCN: 他读古典原著。
senses.why: The best writers of antiquity were the original classics, so their whole world became classical.
senses.whyCN: 上古最优秀的作家原本就是经典，于是他们的整个世界都被称为古典。

senses.title: Of a formal musical tradition
senses.definition: belonging to the serious European musical tradition from about seventeen fifty onwards
senses.definitionCN: 属于十八世纪中叶以来欧洲严肃音乐传统的
senses.example: She grew up listening to classical music.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小听古典音乐。
senses.why: Music that followed the old models of form and balance took the same label as ancient art.
senses.whyCN: 遵循旧有形式与均衡范本的音乐，借用了古代艺术的那个标签。

senses.title: Established as standard
senses.definition: long accepted as the standard form of a subject or method
senses.definitionCN: 长期被接受为某学科或方法的标准形式
senses.example: Classical physics fails at very small scales.
senses.exampleCN: 经典物理学在极小尺度上失效。
senses.why: What is taught as the old standard is called classical, in contrast with newer models.
senses.whyCN: 作为旧有标准被教授的内容被称为经典，以区别于更新的模型。

intro.en: Classical is the adjective of classic and keeps the idea of a first-rank model.
intro.cn: classical 是 classic 的形容词形式，保留了第一流范本的观念。

items.en: Classicus meant of the highest class.
items.cn: classicus 意为最高等级的。

items.en: The best authors were called scriptores classici.
items.cn: 最优秀的作家被称为 scriptores classici。

items.en: Classical first described the best Greek and Latin authors.
items.cn: classical 最初形容最优秀的希腊罗马作家。

items.en: The word spread to architecture, art and then music.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到建筑、艺术，随后又扩展到音乐。

items.en: It now also marks the older standard in science.
items.cn: 它如今也标记科学中的旧有标准。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the classic family, while the meaning group names old and standard traditions.
note.cn: 形近组列出 classic 家族，近义组列出古老与标准传统。

entries.definition: of lasting high quality or very typical
entries.definitionCN: 经久不衰的或非常典型的

entries.definition: a person who studies ancient texts
entries.definitionCN: 研究古代典籍的人

entries.definition: stylish and of good quality
entries.definitionCN: 有格调且品质好的

entries.definition: following customs handed down over time
entries.definitionCN: 遵循世代相传的习俗

entries.definition: belonging to the distant past
entries.definitionCN: 属于遥远过去的

entries.definition: following an official or strict style
entries.definitionCN: 遵循正式或严格风格的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the ancient world, the concert hall and the standard science sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用古代世界、音乐厅与标准科学义。

normal.en: Classical is classic plus -al, so it always describes something rather than naming a work.
normal.cn: classical 是 classic 加 -al，因此总在形容某物，而不是指某部作品。

normal.en: A classic novel is a great book, while classical literature is the literature of Greece and Rome.
normal.cn: a classic novel 指一本好书，classical literature 则指希腊罗马文学。

normal.en: Classical music is a shelf in the record shop, not simply old music.
normal.cn: 古典音乐是唱片店里的一格分类，而不只是老音乐。

normal.en: Classical physics is the physics taught before relativity and quantum theory came along.
normal.cn: 经典物理指相对论与量子论出现之前所教的物理。

normal.en: The -al ending makes a word about a tradition, not about one admired example.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 让词指向一种传统，而非某一件被称赏的作品。

abstract.en: Picture a marble temple front with six columns and a low triangle above.
abstract.cn: 想象一座六根石柱、上方有扁三角的大理石神庙正面。

abstract.en: Picture a string section tuning to a single note before the conductor arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥上台前弦乐组对着一个音调音。

abstract.en: Picture a blackboard of old formulas still used in a modern lesson.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上写满如今课堂仍在使用的旧公式。

examples.en: He reads classical texts in the original.
examples.cn: 他读古典原著。

examples.en: The orchestra opened with a piece of classical music from Vienna.
examples.cn: 乐团以一首维也纳古典乐曲开场。

examples.en: Classical physics fails at very small scales.
examples.cn: 经典物理学在极小尺度上失效。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 classic 想成「一流」，al 想成「的」：属于一流传统的，就是古典的。

root: 源自拉丁语 classicus（最高等级的），由形容一流作家的用法扩展为形容古希腊罗马及其艺术传统。

sensesIntro.en: From the ancient world to its art, then to music, and finally to any established standard.
sensesIntro.cn: 从古代世界到其艺术，再到音乐，最后到任何既定标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marble temple front with balanced columns.
core.cn: 核心意象：比例匀称的石柱神庙正面。

branches.en: The top rank attaches to the ancient world itself.
branches.cn: 最高等级直接附着于古代世界。

branches.en: Music that follows old forms inherits the label.
branches.cn: 遵循旧形式的音乐继承了这个标签。

branches.en: An old standard stays classical beside newer models.
branches.cn: 旧标准在新模型旁仍称经典。

branches.en: Both rest on imitation of ancient models.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在模仿古代范本之上。

branches.en: Old age and high authority combine in one word.
branches.cn: 古老与权威在这个词里合而为一。

intro.en: The adjective adds -al to classic and grows a style noun, an agent noun and a prefix form.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由 classic 加 -al 构成，并长出风格名词、施动名词与前缀形式。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin classicus, so classical and classify share one rank word.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 classicus，因此 classical 与 classify 共用一个等级词。

items.example: The hall is built in a classical style.
items.exampleCN: 这座大厅按古典风格建造。

items.meaningCN: 以古代范本为基础的艺术
items.exampleCN: 这场运动转向古典主义。

items.meaning: a student of the ancient world
items.example: A classicist advised on the text.
items.exampleCN: 一位古典学者为文本提供了意见。

items.example: The bank has a neoclassical front.
items.exampleCN: 这家银行有座新古典风格的正面。

items.example: The car is a classic model.
Classical comes from the word for class.
items.exampleCN: classical 来自表示等级的那个词。

latinEntries.example: Classicus gave both classic and classical.
latinEntries.exampleCN: classicus 同时给出 classic 与 classical。

definition_zh: 分类；归类；类别；（图书等）分类体系
definition_en: the act of putting things into groups, a group formed in this way, or the system used for grouping them
core_image: 抽屉里按标签分格、贴好编号的标本
scene: 标本柜的抽屉上贴着标签，从门到科排得整整齐齐。The classification of these plants took years.
sceneCN: 这里 classification 指「分类」（第 1 个义项：把事物按共同特征归入各组）；句意是给这些植物分类花了好几年。

pos.zh: 分类；归类；类别；分类体系

senses.title: The act of sorting
senses.definition: the act of arranging things into groups according to shared features
senses.definitionCN: 按共同特征把事物归入各组的动作
senses.example: The classification of the finds took a whole winter.
senses.exampleCN: 给这些出土物分类花了整整一个冬天。
senses.why: The noun of action simply names what the verb classify does.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作名词直接指 classify 这个动词所做的事。

senses.title: A group produced by sorting
senses.definition: one of the groups that result from sorting things
senses.definitionCN: 分类之后形成的其中一组
senses.example: These tools fall into a separate classification.
senses.exampleCN: 这些工具属于另一个类别。
senses.why: Once the sorting is finished, each box in the result takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 分类完成后，结果中的每一个格子也叫同一个名字。

senses.title: A system of groups
senses.definition: the whole scheme by which a subject is divided into ordered groups
senses.definitionCN: 把某学科划分成有序各组的整套方案
senses.example: The library uses a simple classification.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆采用一套简单的分类法。
senses.why: A set of related groups becomes a system, and the system keeps the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 相关的各组构成体系，而这个体系仍沿用那个动作的名称。

intro.en: Classification joins the class root to the Latin suffix for making a noun of action.
intro.cn: classification 把 class 词根与拉丁语构成动作名词的后缀结合起来。

items.en: Classis meant a division or a class.
items.cn: classis 意为划分或等级。

items.en: Facere meant to make, so the pair meant to make groups.
items.cn: facere 意为做，两者合起来意为做出分组。

items.en: Classification named the new science of sorting plants.
items.cn: classification 指新兴的植物分类之学。

items.en: English borrowed the word for any ordered grouping.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，指任何有序分组。

items.en: It now covers library systems, jobs and secret files.
items.cn: 它如今涵盖图书系统、职位与机密文件。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the classify family, while the meaning group names the results of sorting.
note.cn: 形近组列出 classify 家族，近义组列出分类的结果。

entries.definition: to arrange things into groups
entries.definitionCN: 把事物编排成组

entries.definition: a person or tool that sorts things
entries.definitionCN: 给事物分类的人或工具

entries.definition: arranged in groups, or officially secret
entries.definitionCN: 已分组的，或官方保密的

entries.definition: a group of things of one kind
entries.definitionCN: 同类事物构成的组

entries.definition: a set of things placed together
entries.definitionCN: 放在一起的一组事物

entries.definition: the act of arranging things by kind
entries.definitionCN: 按种类整理事物的动作

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the class root, the -ification ending and the library image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 class 词根、-ification 后缀与图书馆意象。

normal.en: Classification is class plus -ification, so it is literally the making of classes.
normal.cn: classification 是 class 加 -ification，字面上就是造出类别。

normal.en: The word names three things in turn: the act, one resulting group and the whole system.
normal.cn: 这个词依次指三样东西：动作、一个结果组以及整套体系。

normal.en: Biology lives on classification, from kingdom down to species.
normal.cn: 生物学离不开分类，从界一直到种。

normal.en: A classified document is not sorted; it is marked secret.
normal.cn: a classified document 不是分好类的文件，而是标为机密的文件。

normal.en: The verb is classify, the doer is classifier, the result is classification.
normal.cn: 动词是 classify，执行者是 classifier，结果是 classification。

abstract.en: Picture a cabinet of drawers, each with a printed label and a number.
abstract.cn: 想象一个抽屉柜，每个抽屉都贴着打印标签和编号。

abstract.en: Picture a pile of leaves sorted into two trays by shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆叶子按形状分进两个托盘。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf where every spine carries the same small code.
abstract.cn: 想象图书馆书架，每本书脊上都有同样的小编码。

examples.en: The classification of the finds took a whole winter.
examples.cn: 给这些出土物分类花了整整一个冬天。

examples.en: These tools fall into a separate classification.
examples.cn: 这些工具属于另一个类别。

examples.en: The library uses a simple classification for all its maps.
examples.cn: 这家图书馆对所有地图采用一套简单的分类法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 class 想成「类」，ification 想成「化过程」：把东西归成类的过程，就是分类。

root: 由拉丁语 classis（划分）与 facere（做）组合而成，经法语进入英语，本义是做出分组。

sensesIntro.en: First the act, then a single group, and finally the whole ordered system.
sensesIntro.cn: 先指动作，再指单个组，最后指整套有序体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: labelled drawers holding sorted specimens.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴着标签、装好分类标本的抽屉。

branches.en: The act of sorting is the first meaning.
branches.cn: 分类这个动作是第一层含义。

branches.en: Each finished group takes the same name.
branches.cn: 每个分好的组也叫同一个名字。

branches.en: The set of groups becomes a system.
branches.cn: 各组汇合起来成为体系。

branches.en: The act and its result differ only by a finished edge.
branches.cn: 动作与结果只差一个完成的边界。

branches.en: Groups become a system once their order is fixed.
branches.cn: 各组一旦固定次序就成了体系。

intro.en: The noun base grows a verb, two adjectives and an agent noun.
intro.cn: 这个名词词基长出动词、两个形容词与一个施动名词。

latinIntro.en: The base joins Latin classis, a division, with facere, to make.
latinIntro.cn: 词基把拉丁语 classis（划分）与 facere（做）结合起来。

items.meaning: the act or result of sorting
more than one category or system

items.example: We classify the rocks by origin.
items.exampleCN: 我们按成因给岩石分类。

items.meaningCN: 已分类的，或标为机密的

items.meaning: a person or device that sorts

items.example: Each class has its own label.
items.exampleCN: 每一类都有自己的标签。

latinEntries.exampleCN: classis 是 classification 的开头。

definition_zh: 把……分类；把……归入某类；把（文件）列为机密
definition_en: to arrange things into groups by shared features, or to declare official information secret
core_image: 长桌上摊开的标本被一一放进贴标签的盒子
scene: 管理员把新到的化石摊在长桌上。Scientists classify these shells by shape and age.
sceneCN: 这里 classify 指「把……分类」（第 1 个义项：按共同特征把事物归入各组）；句意是科学家按形状与年代给这些贝壳分类。

senses.title: To sort into groups
senses.definition: to put things into groups according to features they share
senses.definitionCN: 按共同特征把事物放进各组
senses.example: The students classified the leaves by shape.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们按形状给叶子分类。
senses.why: The verb joins the Latin word for a division with the verb to make, so it means to make divisions.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把拉丁语表示划分的词与表示做的动词结合，意为造出划分。

senses.title: To mark information secret
senses.definition: to give official papers a security level that limits who may read them
senses.definitionCN: 给官方文件定下保密等级，限制可阅读的人
senses.example: The report was classified for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告被列为机密三十年。
senses.why: A secret file is placed in a restricted class, so the sorting verb took on this official sense.
senses.whyCN: 机密文件被归入受限的等级，于是这个分类动词带上了官方含义。

intro.en: Classify is a learned compound of the Latin words for a division and for making.
intro.cn: classify 是拉丁语表示划分与表示做的两个词构成的学术复合词。

items.en: Classis meant a division or a class.
items.cn: classis 意为划分或等级。

items.en: Facere meant to make or to do.
items.cn: facere 意为制作或做。

items.en: Classifier named the work of sorting plants and minerals.
items.cn: classifier 指给植物与矿物分类的工作。

items.en: English took classify from the French naturalists.
items.cn: 英语从法国博物学家那里借入 classify。

items.en: The verb also came to mean restricting official papers.
items.cn: 这个动词后来又表示限制官方文件的阅读。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that differ by one or two letters, while the meaning group names sorting actions.
note.cn: 形近组列出只差一两个字母的词，近义组列出分类动作。

entries.definition: to make something easier to understand
entries.definitionCN: 使某事更容易理解

entries.definition: a group or a lesson
entries.definitionCN: 组、等级或一节课

entries.definition: a person or device that sorts things
entries.definitionCN: 给事物分类的人或装置

entries.definition: to put things in order by type
entries.definitionCN: 按种类把事物排好

entries.definition: to place something in a named group
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放进有名称的组

entries.definition: to put things in a planned order
entries.definitionCN: 把事物按计划排好

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the class root, the -ify ending and the two very different senses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 class 词根、-ify 后缀以及两个差别很大的义项。

normal.en: Classify is class plus -ify, so it means to make classes.
normal.cn: classify 是 class 加 -ify，所以意思是造出类别。

normal.en: Classify by and classify as are the two patterns: by a feature, as a member.
normal.cn: classify by 与 classify as 是两个句型：按某特征分，归为某成员。

normal.en: A classified document has a class of secrecy, not a class of students.
normal.cn: a classified document 有保密等级，不是指学生班级。

normal.en: The noun is classification and the doer is classifier, both from the same verb.
normal.cn: 名词是 classification，执行者是 classifier，都出自这个动词。

normal.en: Scientists classify first and name later.
normal.cn: 科学家先分类，后命名。

abstract.en: Picture a long table of shells with small paper labels beside each pile.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌上摆满贝壳，每堆旁边都有小纸标签。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp folder where every page holds one kind only.
abstract.cn: 想象一本邮票册，每一页只放一个种类。

abstract.en: Picture a folder stamped with a red word and locked in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一个盖了红字的文件夹被锁进抽屉。

examples.en: The students classified the leaves by shape.
examples.cn: 学生们按形状给叶子分类。

examples.en: These birds are classified as rare in the region.
examples.cn: 这些鸟在该地区被列为稀有。

examples.en: The report was classified for thirty years.
examples.cn: 这份报告被列为机密三十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 class 想成「类」，ify 想成「使」：使东西各归其类，就是分类。

root: 由拉丁语 classis（划分）与 facere（做）组合，经法语 classifier 进入英语，本义是做出分组。

sensesIntro.en: One verb sorts objects into groups and also puts secret papers into a restricted class.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动词既把实物分进各组，也把机密文件归入受限等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: specimens laid out and moved into labelled boxes.
core.cn: 核心意象：标本摊开来，被逐一移进贴标签的盒子。

branches.en: The verb makes groups out of mixed things.
branches.cn: 这个动词把混杂之物分成组。

branches.en: Official papers are put into a secrecy class.
branches.cn: 官方文件被放进保密等级。

branches.en: Both senses place something inside a class.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是把某物放进某一类。

branches.en: A shared feature is the knife that cuts the groups apart.
branches.cn: 共同特征是切开各组的那把刀。

branches.en: Secrecy is only one class among many.
branches.cn: 保密只是众多类别中的一类。

intro.en: The verb takes -es, -ed and -ing, and feeds the whole classification family.
intro.cn: 这个动词接 -es、-ed、-ing，并衍生出整个 classification 家族。

latinIntro.en: The base pairs Latin classis, a division, with facere, to make.
latinIntro.cn: 词基把拉丁语 classis（划分）与 facere（做）配在一起。

items.example: We classify the samples by age.
items.exampleCN: 我们按年代给样本分类。

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.exampleCN: 她给每件新发现物分类。

items.example: They classified the rocks last week.
items.exampleCN: 他们上周把岩石分了类。

items.meaning: a person or device that sorts

items.exampleCN: 这块碎片几乎无法归类。

items.meaning: forming verbs that mean to make
items.meaningCN: 构成表示使之怎样的动词

latinEntries.example: Facere supplies the second half of classify.
latinEntries.exampleCN: facere 提供了 classify 的后半部分。

definition_zh: 同班同学；同窗
definition_en: a member of the same class at school
core_image: 和你坐同一间教室的同桌伙伴
scene: 新学期第一天，教室里坐满了熟悉的面孔。My classmates helped me carry the new books.
sceneCN: 这里 classmate 是「同班同学」（第 1 个义项：与你在同一班级学习的人）；句意是同学们帮我搬新书。

derivatives.zh: classmate 的基础词，义为「班级；课」
classmate 的构词成分，义为「伙伴；同伴」

senses.title: A student in the same class
senses.definition: a person who studies in the same class as you
senses.definitionCN: 与你在同一班级学习的人
senses.example: Wang Lin is my deskmate and classmate.
senses.exampleCN: 王林是我的同桌兼同班同学。
senses.why: Class plus mate simply names the fellow of your class.
senses.whyCN: class 加 mate，直接命名与你同班的人。

senses.title: A schoolmate of the same year
senses.definition: someone who was at school with you in the same years
senses.definitionCN: 与你同期在校学习过的人
senses.example: I met an old classmate at the bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 我在书店遇到了一位老同学。
senses.why: Years later the same-year link keeps the name alive.
senses.whyCN: 多年以后，同窗之谊仍沿用这个名字。

intro.en: Classmate is a young compound: class plus mate.
intro.cn: classmate 是年轻的复合词：class 加 mate。

items.en: Latin classis meant a ranked division of people.
items.cn: 拉丁语 classis 指人的等级分组。

items.en: English formed class in the seventeenth century from classis.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语由 classis 构成 class。

items.en: Middle English had mette meaning a companion or equal.
items.cn: 中古英语 mette 义为「伙伴；同侪」。

items.en: Mate goes back to Germanic *gamatjon, one sharing food at a table.
items.cn: mate 可追溯到日耳曼语 *gamatjon，指同桌共餐者。

items.en: The compound classmate became common in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 复合词 classmate 在十九世纪普遍使用。

note.en: The first group gathers the -mate family; the second gathers school words.
note.cn: 第一组收 -mate 词族，第二组收校园类词。

entries.definition: A member of the same team.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「队友」，同用 mate 构词。

entries.definition: A person sharing a room.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「室友」，同用 mate 构词。

entries.definition: The room where classes meet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「教室」，词首与 classmate 相同。

entries.definition: A person from the same school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「校友；同学」，范围更大。

entries.definition: The student sitting next to you.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同桌」。

entries.definition: A formal phrase for a student together with you.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「同学」，较正式。

normalIntro.en: Remember classmate as class plus mate.
normalIntro.cn: 把 classmate 记成 class 加 mate。

normal.en: mate means partner or friend.
normal.cn: mate 表示伙伴、朋友。

normal.en: teammate and roommate use the same pattern.
normal.cn: teammate 和 roommate 用同一构词法。

normal.en: a new classmate joins at the term start.
normal.cn: 新学期会有新同学加入。

normal.en: old classmates meet again years later.
normal.cn: 多年后老同学重逢。

normal.en: helping classmates makes friendship.
normal.cn: 帮助同学能增进友谊。

abstract.en: See two schoolbags side by side on one desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一张课桌上并排的两个书包。

abstract.en: Hear whispers about homework between two friends.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见两位好友间讨论作业的耳语。

abstract.en: Feel the joy of meeting an old friend after years.
abstract.cn: 感受多年后重逢老友的喜悦。

examples.en: My classmates and I cleaned the playground.
examples.cn: 我和同学们打扫了操场。

examples.en: A new classmate joined us this term.
examples.cn: 这学期来了一位新同学。

examples.en: She still writes to her classmates from primary school.
examples.cn: 她仍和小学同学通信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克拉斯美特」——克拉斯有个美好特好的同班伙伴。

root: class（拉丁语 classis，等级分组）+ mate（中古英语 mette，伙伴，出自日耳曼语 *gamatjon「同桌共餐者」）→ 现代英语 classmate；同类复合词有 teammate、roommate。

sensesIntro.en: Classmate names your present class fellows and, later, anyone who shared your school years.
sensesIntro.cn: classmate 既指现在的同班同学，也指同窗岁月里的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pupils sharing one classroom
core.cn: 核心意象：共用一间教室的两个学生

branches.en: A current class fellow
branches.cn: 现在的同班同学

branches.en: A same-year schoolmate
branches.cn: 同届同窗

branches.en: A partner in study
branches.cn: 学习上的伙伴

branches.en: A friend built at school
branches.cn: 在学校结下的朋友

branches.en: A face from past years
branches.cn: 往日岁月中的面孔

intro.en: The ending -mate builds a family of companions.
intro.cn: 后缀 -mate 构建了伙伴词族。

latinIntro.en: Mate is Germanic, not Latin, so no Latin entry sits here.
latinIntro.cn: mate 属日耳曼词源，此处无拉丁同族词。

items.example: Pass the ball to a teammate.

items.exampleCN: 她在市区遇到一位校友。

items.example: A book is a good companion.

definition_zh: 从句；分句；（合同、法律的）条款
definition_en: a group of words with its own verb that forms part of a sentence, or a separate condition in a legal document
core_image: 合同上被手指按住的一行小字
scene: 律师把合同推到对面，手指顺着其中一行往下滑。A single clause in the contract decides who pays.
sceneCN: 这里 clause 指「条款」（第 2 个义项：法律文件中的一项独立规定）；句意是合同里的一条条款决定了由谁付款。

senses.title: A part of a sentence
senses.definition: a group of words that contains a verb and forms part of a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 含有动词、构成句子一部分的一组词
senses.example: The sentence has one main clause and two relative clauses.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子有一个主句和两个关系从句。
senses.why: A grammatical clause is a closed unit of meaning, so it took the Latin word for a closing.
senses.whyCN: 语法上的分句是一个闭合的意义单位，因此用了拉丁语表示关闭的词。

senses.title: A condition in a document
senses.definition: a separate item in a contract, treaty or law that states a condition
senses.definitionCN: 合同、条约或法律中规定某项条件的独立条目
senses.example: The contract contains a clause about late payment.
senses.exampleCN: 合同里有一条关于逾期付款的条款。
senses.why: Legal sentences were also divided into closed units, and each item kept the name of a clause.
senses.whyCN: 法律条文同样被分成闭合的单元，每一小条都沿用 clause 之名。

intro.en: Clause comes from a Latin verb meaning to close, and it still means a closed unit of a sentence.
intro.cn: clause 出自拉丁语表示关闭的动词，至今仍指句子中一个闭合的单位。

items.en: Claudere meant to close or shut.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭或合上。

items.en: Clausa meant a closed section of a text.
items.cn: clausa 指文本中闭合的一段。

items.en: Clause carried the legal sense of a proviso.
items.cn: clause 带有条文式的法律含义。

items.en: English used clause in law before it named grammar.
items.cn: 英语先在法律中使用 clause，后用于语法。

items.en: The grammatical sense is now the everyday one.
items.cn: 语法义如今是日常用法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that rhyme or nearly rhyme, while the meaning group names parts of sentences and documents.
note.cn: 形近组列出押韵或近韵的词，近义组列出句子与文件中的成分。

entries.definition: something that makes an event happen
entries.definitionCN: 使某事件发生的原因

entries.definition: a short stop before continuing
entries.definitionCN: 继续之前的短暂停顿

entries.definition: a group of pupils or a lesson
entries.definitionCN: 一群学生或一节课

entries.definition: a small group of words without a full verb
entries.definitionCN: 不含完整动词的一小组词

entries.definition: a condition written into a law or contract
entries.definitionCN: 写入法律或合同的某项条件

entries.definition: one of the parts into which a text is divided
entries.definitionCN: 文本被分成的部分之一

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the closing root, the grammar sense and the contract sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用关闭词根、语法义与合同义。

normal.en: Clause hides the Latin verb to close, so a clause is a closed piece of a sentence.
normal.cn: clause 里藏着拉丁语表示关闭的动词，所以分句是句子里闭合的一块。

normal.en: A clause must have a verb, while a phrase may have none.
normal.cn: 分句必须有动词，短语可以没有。

normal.en: The same word works in grammar and in law, because both divide a text into units.
normal.cn: 同一个词兼用于语法与法律，因为两者都把文本分成单元。

normal.en: An escape clause is a door left open in a contract.
normal.cn: escape clause 是合同里留着一扇开着的门。

normal.en: Clause is one syllable and ends in a soft z sound.
normal.cn: clause 只有一个音节，结尾是柔和的 z 音。

abstract.en: Picture a finger stopping under one short line of small print.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指停在一行小字下面。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence cut into two blocks by a comma.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子被逗号切成两块。

abstract.en: Picture a contract with one paragraph marked in yellow.
abstract.cn: 想象一份合同里有一段被荧光笔标黄。

examples.en: The sentence has one main clause and two relative clauses.
examples.cn: 这个句子有一个主句和两个关系从句。

examples.en: The contract contains a clause about late payment.
examples.cn: 合同里有一条关于逾期付款的条款。

examples.en: They removed the escape clause before signing.
examples.cn: 签约前他们删掉了例外条款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「扣」，ause 想成「奥斯」：一扣扣住的一小段，就是分句或条款。

root: 源自拉丁语 claudere（关闭）的分词形式 clausa（闭合的一段），经中世纪拉丁语与古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A closed unit of a sentence becomes a closed unit of a law, and both keep one name.
sensesIntro.cn: 句子里闭合的一块，后来变成法律中闭合的一条，两者共用一个名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger holding one printed line in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指按住印刷文本上的一行。

branches.en: Grammar closes a sentence into clauses.
branches.cn: 语法把句子切成闭合的分句。

branches.en: Law closes a document into numbered conditions.
branches.cn: 法律把文件切成编号的条件。

branches.en: Both senses name a closed unit of text.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指文本中闭合的单元。

branches.en: A clause needs its own verb, which a phrase lacks.
branches.cn: 分句需要自己的动词，短语则没有。

branches.en: A clause in a contract states one enforceable condition.
branches.cn: 合同中的一条条款规定一项可执行的条件。

intro.en: The noun takes a plural, an adjective and a prefixed form, and shares a root with close and closure.
intro.cn: 这个名词接复数、形容词与前缀形式，并与 close、closure 同根。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin claudere, to close, which also gave close, closure and enclose.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 claudere（关闭），close、closure、enclose 也源于它。

items.meaning: a sentence part or a legal item
items.example: The clause is easy to miss.

items.meaning: a smaller clause inside a clause
items.exampleCN: 这个次级分句补出一个条件。

items.example: The closure of the road lasted a week.

latinEntries.example: Claudere is the root of clause and close.
latinEntries.exampleCN: claudere 是 clause 与 close 的词根。

definition_zh: n. 幽闭恐惧症；对封闭空间的强烈恐惧
definition_en: a strong fear of being in small or enclosed spaces
core_image: 电梯门合拢的一刻，胸口忽然收紧
scene: 电梯门一关上，她就感到一阵幽闭恐惧。She felt a rush of claustrophobia as the lift doors closed.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：claustrophobia 指幽闭恐惧；句意是电梯门一关上，她就感到一阵幽闭恐惧。

derivatives.zh: 幽闭恐惧的；令人压抑的

senses.title: Fear of enclosed spaces
senses.definition: an intense fear of being in small or closed places
senses.definitionCN: 对狭小或封闭场所的强烈恐惧
senses.example: The tiny lift triggered her claustrophobia.
senses.exampleCN: 狭小的电梯引发了她的幽闭恐惧。
senses.why: Latin claustrum means an enclosed place and Greek phobos means fear.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 claustrum 意为封闭处，希腊语 phobos 意为恐惧。

senses.title: A feeling of being trapped
senses.definition: a suffocating sense of being shut in by a situation
senses.definitionCN: 被某种处境困住的窒息感
senses.example: He felt a kind of claustrophobia in his narrow routine.
senses.exampleCN: 他在狭窄的日常里有一种被困住的压抑。
senses.why: Fear of closed rooms widened to closed lives.
senses.whyCN: 对封闭房间的恐惧扩展到了封闭的生活。

intro.en: The word joins a Latin room to a Greek fear and was coined for medicine.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语的「房间」和希腊语的「恐惧」结合，为医学而造。

items.en: Claustrum means a lock, a bolt or an enclosed place.
items.cn: claustrum 意为锁、门闩或封闭处。

items.en: Phobos means fear or panic.
items.cn: phobos 意为恐惧、惊惶。

items.en: Psychiatrists build the term for fear of closed rooms.
items.cn: 1879 年精神科医生造出此词，指对封闭房间的恐惧。

items.en: The word passes from clinics into daily speech.
items.cn: 二十世纪该词从诊所进入日常语言。

items.en: It now also names the feeling of a shut-in life.
items.cn: 现代也指被封闭生活困住的感觉。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -phobia shape; the near-meaning group names other phobias and fears.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -phobia 词形；近义组列出其他恐惧症与恐惧。

entries.definition: Fear of open or crowded places.
entries.definitionCN: 广场恐惧症。

entries.definition: Fear or dislike of foreigners.
entries.definitionCN: 排外恐惧。

entries.definition: Causing or feeling this fear.
entries.definitionCN: 引起幽闭恐惧的。

entries.definition: A strong unreasonable fear.
entries.definitionCN: 恐惧症。

entries.definition: A lasting feeling of worry.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑。

entries.definition: Great fear of something coming.
entries.definitionCN: 畏惧。

normalIntro.en: Claustrum is a closed room and phobos is fear: a room that frightens.
normalIntro.cn: claustrum 是封闭房间，phobos 是恐惧：一间吓人的屋子。

normal.en: Claustro means closed.
normal.cn: claustro 意为封闭。

normal.en: Phobia means fear.
normal.cn: phobia 意为恐惧。

normal.en: A lift is a moving closed room.
normal.cn: 电梯是会移动的封闭房间。

normal.en: The fear arrives when the doors shut.
normal.cn: 门一关，恐惧就来。

normal.en: The word can also picture a narrow life.
normal.cn: 这个词也能形容狭窄的生活。

abstract.en: Walls that move closer.
abstract.cn: 不断逼近的墙。

abstract.en: Fear with a locked door.
abstract.cn: 锁着门的恐惧。

abstract.en: Air that forgets to circulate.
abstract.cn: 忘了流动的空气。

examples.en: His claustrophobia makes tunnels difficult for him.
examples.cn: 他的幽闭恐惧让他难以忍受隧道。

examples.en: She stood near the exit to fight her claustrophobia.
examples.cn: 她站在出口附近，对抗自己的幽闭恐惧。

examples.en: The small village gave him a strange claustrophobia.
examples.cn: 这个小村庄让他有一种奇怪的被困感。

dict_mnemonic.text: claustro（封闭）+ phobia（恐惧）→ 对封闭空间的恐惧。

root: 拉丁 claustrum（封闭处）+ 希腊 phobos（恐惧）→ 医学新造词 claustrophobia

sensesIntro.en: A door that shuts becomes a metaphor for a life that closes.
sensesIntro.cn: 关上的门，成了封闭生活的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lift doors meeting in front of a face
core.cn: 核心意象：两扇电梯门在眼前合拢

branches.en: A lift door sliding shut.
branches.cn: 缓缓合上的电梯门。

branches.en: A tunnel with no light behind.
branches.cn: 身后无光的隧道。

branches.en: A small routine that will not open.
branches.cn: 打不开的狭小日常。

branches.en: A crowded room with no exit in sight.
branches.cn: 看不见出口的拥挤房间。

branches.en: A closed place and a closed life.
branches.cn: 封闭的场所与封闭的生活。

intro.en: Claustrophobia is built from a Latin room and a Greek fear; the list adds those pieces.
intro.cn: claustrophobia 由拉丁「房间」与希腊「恐惧」构成；下面列出这些成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin claustrum is a bolt, claudere is to shut, and Greek phobos is fear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 claustrum 意为门闩，claudere 意为关闭，希腊语 phobos 意为恐惧。

latinEntries.exampleCN: claustrum 产生 claustrophobia 与 cloister。
claudere 产生 exclude 与 include。
phobos 产生 phobia 与 phobic。

definition_zh: 黏土；陶土；（网球）红土场地
definition_en: heavy sticky earth that can be shaped when wet and baked hard, or a sports surface made of crushed clay
core_image: 转盘上被手指拉高的湿泥坯
scene: 轮盘转起来，手上沾满湿乎乎的土。She pressed a lump of clay into a shallow bowl.
sceneCN: 这里 clay 指「黏土」（第 1 个义项：湿时可塑、烧后变硬的黏性土）；句意是她把一团黏土按成了一个浅碗。

senses.title: Sticky earth for shaping
senses.definition: a heavy sticky earth that becomes soft when wet and hard when baked
senses.definitionCN: 湿时变软、烧后变硬的厚重黏性土
senses.example: The children shaped animals from clay.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们用黏土捏动物。
senses.why: The old English word named exactly this sticky earth, and that sense has never changed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语中的这个词正是指这种黏性土，这一含义从未改变。

senses.title: A crushed-clay sports surface
senses.definition: a tennis court surface made of crushed brick or clay
senses.definitionCN: 用碎砖或黏土铺成的网球场地面
senses.example: He plays best on clay.
senses.exampleCN: 他在红土场上打得最好。
senses.why: Players shortened the name of the clay court until the material alone meant the surface.
senses.whyCN: 球员把红土球场的名称缩短，最后材料名本身就指这种场地。

intro.en: Clay is a native English word for sticky earth, with relatives across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: clay 是英语本族词，指黏性土，在日耳曼诸语言中有同源词。

items.en: Clæg meant sticky earth used by potters.
items.cn: clæg 指陶工使用的黏性土。

items.en: The spelling settled as clay.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 clay。

items.en: Writers used clay for the human body in religious prose.
items.cn: 作家在宗教文章中用 clay 指人的身体。

items.en: Brick and tile works made clay a trade word.
items.cn: 砖瓦业使 clay 成为行业词。

items.en: Sports also gave the word a surface sense.
items.cn: 体育又给了这个词场地义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words with a similar vowel or ending, while the meaning group names kinds of earth.
note.cn: 形近组列出元音或结尾相近的短词，近义组列出各种泥土。

entries.definition: to become too sweet or too much
entries.definitionCN: 变得过甜或令人腻烦

entries.definition: to kill someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 杀死某人或某物

entries.definition: a sharp curved nail
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲的尖爪

entries.definition: wet earth that sticks to your shoes
entries.definitionCN: 会粘在鞋上的湿泥

entries.definition: the top layer of earth where plants grow
entries.definitionCN: 植物生长的地表土层

entries.definition: the substance of the ground
entries.definitionCN: 地面的物质

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the potter's wheel, the brick kiln and the red court.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用陶轮、砖窑与红土球场。

normal.en: Clay is what a potter's hands are covered with at the end of the day.
normal.cn: clay 就是陶艺师收工时满手沾着的东西。

normal.en: Wet clay bends, dry clay cracks, fired clay rings.
normal.cn: 湿黏土会弯，干黏土会裂，烧过的陶会响。

normal.en: Clay and clod share a shape and both mean lumpy earth.
normal.cn: clay 与 clod 外形相近，都指成块的土。

normal.en: A clay court is red because crushed brick is mixed in.
normal.cn: 红土球场之所以发红，是因为掺了碎砖。

normal.en: Clay is uncountable, so one says a lump of clay.
normal.cn: clay 不可数，所以说 a lump of clay。

abstract.en: Picture a wet grey cylinder rising under two fingers on a spinning wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象转盘上湿灰的泥柱在两根手指间升高。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of unglazed pots drying in the shade.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上摆着一排未上釉的陶罐在阴处晾干。

abstract.en: Picture a red tennis court with white lines and a sliding player.
abstract.cn: 想象一片画着白线的红土球场，一名球员正在滑步。

examples.en: The children shaped animals from clay.
examples.cn: 孩子们用黏土捏动物。

examples.en: She pressed a lump of clay into a shallow bowl.
examples.cn: 她把一团黏土按成了一个浅碗。

examples.en: He plays best on clay in the spring.
examples.cn: 春天他在红土场上打得最好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「粘」，ay 想成「哎」：粘手得让人哎一声的土，就是黏土。

root: 源自古英语 clæg（黏性土、陶土），与荷兰语 klei、德语 Klei 同源，本义一直保持至今。

sensesIntro.en: Sticky earth for pots first, then the crushed material that makes a court surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 先指做陶器的黏性土，再指铺球场的那种碎料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet clay cylinder rising on a potter's wheel.
core.cn: 核心意象：陶轮上湿黏土被拉高的圆柱。

branches.en: Sticky earth is shaped by hands and then baked.
branches.cn: 黏性土被手塑形，再经火烧。

branches.en: Crushed clay becomes a sports surface.
branches.cn: 碎黏土成了运动场地。

branches.en: The material sense underlies the surface sense.
branches.cn: 材料义是场地义的基础。

branches.en: Pottery, bricks and tiles all begin with this word.
branches.cn: 陶器、砖与瓦都从这个词开始。

branches.en: The court is named by what it is made of.
branches.cn: 这种场地以它的材料命名。

intro.en: The noun takes a plural-free form and grows two derived words.
intro.cn: 这个名词没有复数形式，只长出两个派生词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base: clay is a native Germanic word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语词基：clay 是日耳曼语本族词。

items.meaningCN: 用黏土人偶制作的动画
items.exampleCN: 这部影片用了黏土动画。

items.meaning: a pot made of baked clay
items.example: The clay pot keeps the water cool.

items.meaning: soil with a lot of clay in it
items.example: Roses grow well in clay soil.
items.exampleCN: 月季在黏质土里长得好。

items.meaning: a tennis court of crushed clay

definition_zh: 干净的；清洁的；彻底的；打扫；清洗
definition_en: free from dirt or marks, complete and thorough, or to remove dirt from something
core_image: 擦过后能照出窗影的桌面
scene: 客人按门铃前，她把最后一本书塞回书架。She wiped the table until it was clean.
sceneCN: 这里 clean 指「干净的」（第 1 个义项：没有污垢或痕迹）；句意是她把桌子擦到干干净净。

senses.title: Free from dirt
senses.definition: not marked or covered with dirt, and safe to use
senses.definitionCN: 没有污迹或污垢、可以放心使用的
senses.example: Wash your hands and keep the kitchen clean.
senses.exampleCN: 洗手，并保持厨房干净。
senses.why: The old English adjective meant free from dirt and also pure, and both senses travelled together.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语形容词既指没有污垢，也指纯净，两个含义一路同行。

senses.title: To remove dirt
senses.definition: to remove dirt from something by washing or wiping
senses.definitionCN: 通过洗或擦去除某物上的污垢
senses.example: He cleaned the windows before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭前他把窗户擦了。
senses.why: The adjective turned into a verb meaning to make something clean.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转为动词，意为使某物变干净。

senses.title: Complete and thorough
senses.definition: done fully, with nothing left out or hidden
senses.definitionCN: 做得彻底，没有遗漏也没有隐瞒
senses.example: The team made a clean break with the old plan.
senses.exampleCN: 团队与旧方案彻底断了关系。
senses.why: Something clean has nothing sticking to it, so a clean break leaves no loose ends.
senses.whyCN: 干净的东西不粘带杂物，因此 clean break 指不留尾巴的切割。

intro.en: Clean is an old English adjective meaning free of dirt and also pure or clear.
intro.cn: clean 是古英语形容词，既指没有污垢，也指纯净、清楚。

items.en: Clæne meant clean, pure and clear.
items.cn: clæne 意为干净的、纯净的、清楚的。

items.en: The word kept the physical and moral senses together.
items.cn: 这个词把物质义与道德义保留在一起。

items.en: The verb clean appeared, meaning to make clean.
items.cn: 动词 clean 出现，意为使干净。

items.en: Clean up became a common phrase for tidying.
items.cn: clean up 成为表示收拾整理的常用短语。

items.en: The word now also describes energy and technology.
items.cn: 这个词如今也形容能源与技术。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in spelling, while the meaning group names states of order and purity.
note.cn: 形近组列出拼写接近的词，近义组列出整洁与纯净的状态。

entries.definition: easy to see through or to understand
entries.definitionCN: 容易看透或容易理解的

entries.definition: to clean something thoroughly, often the skin
entries.definitionCN: 彻底清洁，常指皮肤

entries.definition: in a neat and skilful way
entries.definitionCN: 干净利落地

entries.definition: arranged neatly with everything in place
entries.definitionCN: 一切归位、摆放整齐的

entries.definition: not mixed with anything harmful
entries.definitionCN: 没有混入有害物的

entries.definition: to clean something with water
entries.definitionCN: 用水清洁某物

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the wiped surface, the verb pair and the thorough sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用擦净的表面、名动搭配与彻底义。

normal.en: Clean is one syllable with a long vowel, so it sounds like a wiped surface shining.
normal.cn: clean 是长元音的单音节词，听起来像擦净的桌面在发亮。

normal.en: The adjective and the verb are identical: a clean room, to clean a room.
normal.cn: 形容词与动词同形：a clean room 与 to clean a room。

normal.en: Clean up is for mess, clean out is for a cupboard, clean off is for a surface.
normal.cn: clean up 收拾乱局，clean out 清空柜子，clean off 擦净表面。

normal.en: A clean break leaves no shared habit behind.
normal.cn: clean break 指不留下共同习惯的彻底了断。

normal.en: Clean energy is energy that leaves no dirt behind.
normal.cn: clean energy 指不留下污物的能源。

abstract.en: Picture a table wiped so well that the window appears in it.
abstract.cn: 想象桌面被擦到能映出窗户。

abstract.en: Picture a white cup upside down on a dry rack.
abstract.cn: 想象一只倒扣在沥水架上的白杯子。

abstract.en: Picture a knife cut through paper with no ragged edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一刀切过纸面，边缘没有毛刺。

examples.en: Wash your hands and keep the kitchen clean.
examples.cn: 洗手，并保持厨房干净。

examples.en: He cleaned the windows before lunch.
examples.cn: 午饭前他把窗户擦了。

examples.en: The team made a clean break with the old plan.
examples.cn: 团队与旧方案彻底断了关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「擦」，ean 想成「亮」：一擦就亮，就是干净。

root: 源自古英语 clæne（没有污垢的、纯净的、清楚的），与德语 klein 的古老含义相关，后由形容词生出动词用法。

sensesIntro.en: Free of dirt becomes an action, and then the idea of leaving nothing behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 没有污垢先是状态，再变成动作，最后引申为不留残余。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wiped table reflecting the window.
core.cn: 核心意象：擦净的桌面映出窗户。

branches.en: The adjective names a surface with nothing on it.
branches.cn: 形容词指表面没有任何附着物。

branches.en: The verb names the work of removing dirt.
branches.cn: 动词指去除污垢的劳动。

branches.en: Nothing left over becomes a thorough break.
branches.cn: 不留残余引申为彻底了断。

branches.en: State and action differ only by the work in between.
branches.cn: 状态与动作只差中间那段劳动。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the absence of anything extra.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在没有多余之物上。

intro.en: One short adjective grows a comparative, a verb set and four derived nouns and adverbs.
intro.cn: 一个短形容词长出比较级、一整套动词形式以及四个派生名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base: clean is a native English word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语词基：clean 是英语本族词。

items.meaning: free of dirt or to remove dirt

items.example: It is the cleanest room in the house.
items.exampleCN: 这是家里最干净的房间。

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.example: She cleans the board every evening.
They cleaned the hall on Friday.
The kitchen is praised for its cleanliness.
items.exampleCN: 这间厨房因干净而受称赞。

items.meaning: in a neat and skilful way

definition_zh: v. 攥紧（拳头）；咬紧（牙关）；紧紧握住
definition_en: to close your hand or teeth tightly, or hold something very firmly
core_image: 愤怒时拳头一寸寸收紧
scene: 她气得攥紧了拳头，一句话也没说。She clenched her fists in anger and said nothing.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：clench 指攥紧拳头；句意是她气得攥紧了拳头，一句话也没说。

senses.title: To close the hand tightly
senses.definition: to curl the fingers into a hard fist
senses.definitionCN: 把手指紧紧握成硬拳
senses.example: She clenched her fists and stepped forward.
senses.exampleCN: 她攥紧拳头走上前。
senses.why: Old English clencan means to hold fast.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 clencan 意为抓紧。

senses.title: To set the teeth or jaw
senses.definition: to press the teeth together hard, often in pain or anger
senses.definitionCN: 常因疼痛或愤怒而用力咬合牙关
senses.example: He clenched his jaw and kept silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他咬紧牙关，一声不吭。
senses.why: The grip of the fist moved to the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 握拳的用力转移到了嘴上。

senses.title: To hold something firmly
senses.definition: to grip an object and refuse to let it go
senses.definitionCN: 抓住某物不肯松手
senses.example: She clenched the letter until it crumpled.
senses.exampleCN: 她把信攥得皱成一团。
senses.why: A closing hand also means a kept object.
senses.whyCN: 合拢的手也意味着抓住的东西。

intro.en: Clench is an old English verb of holding fast that moved from fists to jaws.
intro.cn: clench 是表示抓紧的古英语动词，从拳头延伸到牙关。

items.en: Clencan means to hold fast or clinch.
items.cn: clencan 意为紧握、扣紧。

items.en: Clenched appears as a past form of gripping.
items.cn: 中古英语 clenched 表示抓紧过的。

items.en: Writers describe clenched fists in anger.
items.cn: 十六世纪作家描写愤怒时握紧的拳头。

items.en: Clenched teeth become a set phrase for endurance.
items.cn: 十九世纪「咬紧牙关」成为忍受的固定说法。

items.en: The verb covers hands, teeth and gripped objects.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖手、牙与紧握之物。

note.en: The look-alike group is a near spelling; the near-meaning group names other kinds of tight holding.
note.cn: 形近组是相近拼写；近义组列出其他紧握的说法。

entries.definition: To settle a deal or grapple close.
entries.definitionCN: 敲定；扭打。

entries.definition: To hold something tightly.
entries.definitionCN: 紧抓。

entries.definition: A hook that holds two parts together.
entries.definitionCN: 扣住两部分的钩扣。

entries.definition: To hold something firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 紧握。

entries.definition: To take hold of something.
entries.definitionCN: 抓住。

entries.definition: To make something tighter.
entries.definitionCN: 收紧。

normalIntro.en: A clenched hand is a lock made of fingers.
normalIntro.cn: 攥紧的手就是用手指做成的锁。

normal.en: Clench sounds like a latch snapping shut.
normal.cn: clench 听起来像门闩咔地扣上。

normal.en: Fingers curl into a fist.
normal.cn: 手指蜷成拳头。

normal.en: Teeth clench in pain.
normal.cn: 疼痛时咬紧牙。

normal.en: A hand can clench a letter.
normal.cn: 手能把信攥紧。

normal.en: Clinch is the close cousin.
normal.cn: clinch 是近亲词。

abstract.en: Anger given a shape.
abstract.cn: 被赋予形状的愤怒。

abstract.en: A hand saying no.
abstract.cn: 一只说「不」的手。

abstract.en: Strength pressed into a small space.
abstract.cn: 压在狭小空间里的力量。

examples.en: He clenched his fist behind his back.
examples.cn: 他在背后握紧了拳头。

examples.en: The patient clenched her teeth against the pain.
examples.cn: 病人咬紧牙关忍痛。

examples.en: She clenched the railing as the bus turned.
examples.cn: 公交车转弯时她紧紧抓住扶手。

dict_mnemonic.text: clench 的读音像关节「咔」地收紧：拳、牙、手一起用力。

root: 古英语 clencan（抓紧、扣紧）→ 中古英语 clenchen → 现代 clench

sensesIntro.en: One verb of shutting covers a fist, a jaw and a gripped object.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「合紧」动词涵盖拳头、牙关与紧握之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: knuckles whitening in a closed fist
core.cn: 核心意象：握紧的拳头指节发白

branches.en: A fist raised at a protest.
branches.cn: 抗议中举起的拳头。

branches.en: A jaw locked in pain.
branches.cn: 因疼痛咬紧的下颌。

branches.en: A letter crushed in a hand.
branches.cn: 被手攥皱的信。

branches.en: Fingers round a bus railing.
branches.cn: 抓着公交扶手的手指。

branches.en: Tension held in hand and mouth.
branches.cn: 握在手与嘴里的紧张。

intro.en: Clench is a Germanic word of gripping; the list adds words of holding and drawing tight.
intro.cn: clench 是日耳曼语系的抓紧词；下面列出握持与绷紧词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere is to draw tight, tenere is to hold, and firmare is to make firm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere 意为拉紧，tenere 意为握住，firmare 意为使牢固。

latinEntries.exampleCN: stringere 产生 strict 与 restrict。
tenere 产生 tense 与 tenant。
firmare 产生 firm 与 confirm。

definition_zh: n. （总称）神职人员，教士阶层
definition_en: the priests and other ordained leaders of a religion, taken as a group
core_image: 教堂里一排穿长袍、主持仪式的人
scene: 主日礼拜时，全体神职人员走在队伍最前面。The clergy led the procession at the Sunday service.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：clergy 指神职人员总称；句意是主日礼拜时，全体神职人员走在队伍最前面。

senses.title: Ordained religious leaders as a body
senses.definition: the priests or ministers of a church considered as one group
senses.definitionCN: 被视为一个整体的教会圣职人员
senses.example: The clergy wore black robes for the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 神职人员为葬礼穿黑色长袍。
senses.why: Greek kleros means a lot or heritage, chosen for service.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kleros 意为抽签所得的份，指被选担任圣职。

senses.title: The ordained class of a society
senses.definition: the ordained leaders seen as a social or historical class
senses.definitionCN: 作为社会或历史阶层看待的圣职人员
senses.example: In medieval times the clergy owned much land.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪神职人员拥有大量土地。
senses.why: The group sense became a class in history.
senses.whyCN: 群体义在历史叙述中成为阶层。

intro.en: Clergy begins with a Greek word for a allotted share and becomes the name of an ordained class.
intro.cn: clergy 始于希腊语「抽签所得的份」，后来成为圣职阶层的名称。

items.en: Kleros means a lot or an allotted heritage.
items.cn: kleros 意为抽签所得的份或产业。

items.en: Clericus means a cleric, one of the Lord s lot.
items.cn: clericus 意为圣职人员。

items.en: Clergy names the learned men of the church.
items.cn: 十三世纪 clergy 指教会中通晓文字的人。

items.en: Clergy is set against laity in church debate.
items.cn: 十六世纪宗教改革中，clergy 与 laity 对举。

items.en: The word now covers ordained leaders of many faiths.
items.cn: 现代该词涵盖多种宗教的圣职者。

note.en: The look-alike group is one letter from clergy; the near-meaning group names religious roles.
note.cn: 形近组与 clergy 只差一个字母；近义组列出宗教角色。

entries.definition: A person who keeps records or serves customers.
entries.definitionCN: 职员。

entries.definition: Relating to the clergy or to office work.
entries.definitionCN: 神职的；文书的。

entries.definition: A single ordained person.
entries.definitionCN: 一名圣职人员。

entries.definition: Church members who are not clergy.
entries.definitionCN: 平信徒。

entries.definition: The office or body of priests.
entries.definitionCN: 司祭职。

entries.definition: The work of a religious leader.
entries.definitionCN: 牧职。

normalIntro.en: Clergy is a crowd word: many ordained people seen as one body.
normalIntro.cn: clergy 是集合词：许多圣职者被视为一个整体。

normal.en: Clergy is always plural in feel.
normal.cn: clergy 在感觉上总是集合的。

normal.en: One person is a cleric.
normal.cn: 一个人叫 cleric。

normal.en: The adjective is clerical.
normal.cn: 形容词是 clerical。

normal.en: Clergy and laity are a pair.
normal.cn: clergy 与 laity 是一对。

normal.en: A clergyman is one member.
normal.cn: clergyman 是一名成员。

abstract.en: A row of robes walking together.
abstract.cn: 一排一同行走的长袍。

abstract.en: A class defined by a calling.
abstract.cn: 由召唤定义的阶层。

abstract.en: Voices that speak for a congregation.
abstract.cn: 代会众发声的一群人。

examples.en: The clergy gathered to discuss the new hymn book.
examples.cn: 神职人员聚在一起讨论新的赞美诗集。

examples.en: Many members of the clergy joined the march.
examples.cn: 许多神职人员加入了游行。

examples.en: The clergy and the laity disagreed over the plan.
examples.cn: 神职人员与平信徒对这项计划意见不一。

dict_mnemonic.text: cleric（圣职人员）+ -gy（集合）→ 神职人员这一群体。

root: 希腊 kleros（抽签所得之份）→ 拉丁 clericus（圣职者）→ 英语 clergy

sensesIntro.en: One word names a group of people and, in histories, a whole class.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既指一群人，也指历史中的一个阶层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of robed figures at the front of a church
core.cn: 核心意象：教堂前排一列穿袍的人

branches.en: Robed leaders in a procession.
branches.cn: 队伍中穿袍的领袖。

branches.en: Ministers sharing a hymn book.
branches.cn: 共用一本赞美诗的神职者。

branches.en: A medieval class holding land.
branches.cn: 中世纪占有土地的阶层。

branches.en: Clergy set against laity in debate.
branches.cn: 辩论中与平信徒相对的神职界。

branches.en: A body of people and a rank in history.
branches.cn: 一群人，也是历史中的一个等级。

intro.en: Clergy grows from words of lot, calling and church; the list adds that family.
intro.cn: clergy 由「抽签之份、召唤、教会」词族生长而来；下面列出这些词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek kleros is a lot, Latin clericus is a cleric, and laicus is a lay person.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kleros 意为抽签之份，拉丁语 clericus 意为圣职者，laicus 意为平信徒。

latinEntries.exampleCN: clericus 产生 clergy 与 clerical。
kleros 产生 cleric 与 clergy。
laicus 产生 laity 与 lay。

definition_zh: 职员；办事员；店员；售货员
definition_en: a person who keeps records or does office work, or a person who serves customers in a shop
core_image: 柜台后低头抄写、核对的账本
scene: 柜台前排了几个人，机打的单据一张张吐出来。The bank clerk counted the notes twice.
sceneCN: 这里 clerk 指「职员」（第 1 个义项：在办公室或柜台处理记录与事务的人）；句意是那位银行职员把钞票点了两遍。

senses.title: A person who keeps records
senses.definition: a person employed to keep records, file papers or do other office work
senses.definitionCN: 受雇保管记录、整理文件或做其他办公室事务的人
senses.example: The clerk stamped the form and filed it.
senses.exampleCN: 那位职员在表格上盖了章并归档。
senses.why: The word once meant a clergyman, then any person who could read and write, and later an office worker.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾指教士，后指任何会读写的人，再后来指办公室职员。

senses.title: A shop assistant
senses.definition: a person who serves customers behind a counter, especially in American use
senses.definitionCN: 在柜台后接待顾客的人，尤用于美式英语
senses.example: The clerk wrapped the gift in blue paper.
senses.exampleCN: 店员用蓝纸把礼物包好。
senses.why: Selling behind a counter was also record work, so the same word covered shop staff.
senses.whyCN: 柜台后卖货同样涉及记账，于是同一个词也指店员。

intro.en: Clerk began as the word for a clergyman, since clergy were almost the only people who could read and write.
intro.cn: clerk 起初指教士，因为当时几乎只有教士会读写。

items.en: Kleros meant a lot or a share, including a share of church duty.
items.cn: kleros 意为抽签所得的一份，也包括教会职务的一份。

items.en: Clericus meant a man of the church.
items.cn: clericus 指教会中人。

items.en: Cleric named a priest or a scholar.
items.cn: cleric 指教士或学者。

items.en: Clerk meant a scholar or a secretary, then any office worker.
items.cn: clerk 指学者或书记，后指任何办公人员。

items.en: American use added the shop assistant sense.
items.cn: 美式用法又加上了店员义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds church and writing words, while the meaning group names people who serve at a counter or desk.
note.cn: 形近组列出教会与文书类词，近义组列出在柜台或桌前服务的人。

entries.definition: relating to office work or to clergy
entries.definitionCN: 与办公室工作或教士有关的

entries.definition: the body of people trained for religious work
entries.definitionCN: 受过宗教训练的人员群体

entries.definition: easy to see or understand
entries.definitionCN: 容易看见或理解的

entries.definition: a person who helps someone else at work
entries.definitionCN: 在工作中帮助他人的人

entries.definition: a person who greets visitors at a front desk
entries.definitionCN: 在前台接待来访者的人

entries.definition: a bank worker who handles money at a counter
entries.definitionCN: 在柜台处理现金的银行职员

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the clergy origin, the reading skill and the counter picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用教士来源、读写能力与柜台画面。

normal.en: Clerk and clergy share a root: the clerk was the church's reader and writer.
normal.cn: clerk 与 clergy 同根：当年的 clerk 就是教会里读写的人。

normal.en: Because clerks could read, the word came to mean any keeper of records.
normal.cn: 因为 clerk 会读写，这个词后来指任何管记录的人。

normal.en: In Britain a clerk sits in an office; in America a clerk often stands at a shop counter.
normal.cn: 在英国 clerk 多坐办公室，在美国常站在商店柜台后。

normal.en: The British say klark and the Americans say klerk, and both spell it clerk.
normal.cn: 英音读 klark，美音读 klerk，拼写都是 clerk。

normal.en: Clerical work means paperwork, not church work, in most modern offices.
normal.cn: 在多数现代办公室里，clerical work 指文书工作而非教会工作。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger, an ink pad and a rubber stamp on a high desk.
abstract.cn: 想象高桌上放着账本、印泥和一枚橡皮章。

abstract.en: Picture a queue of people and a printer spitting out receipts.
abstract.cn: 想象排着队的顾客和一台不断吐出单据的打印机。

abstract.en: Picture a man in a black coat copying a letter by hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一位穿黑衣的人手抄一封信。

examples.en: The clerk stamped the form and filed it.
examples.cn: 那位职员在表格上盖了章并归档。

examples.en: The bank clerk counted the notes twice.
examples.cn: 那位银行职员把钞票点了两遍。

examples.en: The clerk wrapped the gift in blue paper.
examples.cn: 店员用蓝纸把礼物包好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「抄」，erk 想成「额」：低头抄到额头出汗的人，就是职员。

root: 源自希腊语 kleros（抽签所得的一份）经拉丁语 clericus（教会中人）进入英语，由教士义转为会读写的人，再转为职员。

sensesIntro.en: A clergyman becomes a literate secretary, then an office worker, then a shop assistant.
sensesIntro.cn: 教士先变成会写字的书记，再变成办公室职员，最后指店员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger, an ink pad and a stamp on a high desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：高桌上的账本、印泥与图章。

branches.en: The record keeper sits at a desk with paper.
branches.cn: 管记录的人坐在桌前与纸打交道。

branches.en: The counter worker serves customers and keeps accounts.
branches.cn: 柜台人员接待顾客并记账。

branches.en: Both senses rest on handling papers and figures.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在处理单据与数字上。

branches.en: Reading and writing were once the clerk's special skill.
branches.cn: 读写曾是 clerk 的独门本事。

branches.en: The American shop sense grew from counter paperwork.
branches.cn: 美式的店员义从柜台记账发展而来。

intro.en: The noun takes a plural and grows an adjective and two nouns of role.
intro.cn: 这个名词接复数，并长出形容词与两个身份名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin clericus, a churchman, from Greek kleros, a lot or share.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 clericus（教会中人），源自希腊语 kleros（一份）。

items.meaningCN: 办公室或商店的工作人员
items.example: The clerk asked for my name.
items.exampleCN: 那位职员问了我的名字。
三名职员共用这个柜台。

items.example: He took a clerkship in the city.
items.exampleCN: 他在城里谋得一个文员职位。

items.meaning: like a clerk or a scholar
items.example: He had a clerkly way with papers.
items.exampleCN: 他处理文件很有文员的样子。

items.example: The clergy once kept the records.

items.exampleCN: 这位神职人员签了登记册。

latinEntries.example: Clericus is the source of clerk.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clericus 是 clerk 的来源。

definition_zh: 点击；发出咔嗒声；突然明白
definition_en: to press a button on a mouse or other device, to make a short sharp sound, or to become suddenly clear in the mind
core_image: 手指按下鼠标键时那一声轻脆的咔嗒
scene: 她把光标移到图标上，手腕轻轻一动。Click the green button to start the test.
sceneCN: 这里 click 指「点击」（第 1 个义项：按下鼠标键）；句意是点击绿色按钮开始测试。

senses.title: Press a mouse button
senses.definition: to press a button on a computer mouse in order to choose something
senses.definitionCN: 按下电脑鼠标的按键以选中某个对象
senses.example: Click the blue button to save your work.
senses.exampleCN: 点击蓝色按钮保存你的工作。
senses.why: The mouse answers with a small snap, so the action took the name of its own sound.
senses.whyCN: 鼠标按下时会发出一声轻响，于是动作借用了自己发出的声音。

senses.title: Short sharp sound
senses.definition: a short sharp sound made when two hard things touch
senses.definitionCN: 两个硬物相碰时发出的短促声响
senses.example: The click of the latch told her that the door was shut.
senses.exampleCN: 门闩的咔嗒声告诉她门已关好。
senses.why: Long before computers, the word belonged to locks, switches and heels.
senses.whyCN: 在计算机出现以前很久，这个词属于锁、开关和鞋跟。

senses.title: Sudden understanding
senses.definition: to become suddenly clear or easy to understand
senses.definitionCN: 突然变得清楚、容易理解
senses.example: Her explanation made the whole rule click.
senses.exampleCN: 她的解释让整条规则一下子通了。
senses.why: A thought seems to snap into place like a latch, so the sound image moved into the mind.
senses.whyCN: 思路像锁扣一样咔一下合上，声音意象便迁移到了头脑中。

intro.en: Click is not borrowed from Latin or Greek; it simply imitates a small sharp noise.
intro.cn: click 并非借自拉丁语或希腊语，它只是模仿一种短促的脆响。

items.en: The word copies the sound of a latch, a key or a small hammer.
items.cn: 这个词模仿门闩、钥匙或小锤发出的声音。

items.en: Click first named the sound made by locks and clock parts.
items.cn: click 最初指锁与钟表零件发出的声响。

items.en: Switches, heels and typewriters widened the range of the sound.
items.cn: 开关、鞋跟与打字机扩大了这种声音的适用范围。

items.en: The computer mouse gave the word a new everyday action.
items.cn: 电脑鼠标赋予这个词一个全新的日常动作。

items.en: The verb now also means to understand something suddenly.
items.cn: 这个动词如今还表示突然理解某事。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short sound words, while the meaning group names actions and noises of touching.
note.cn: 形近组收的是一批短小的拟声词，近义组列出触碰与声响类动作。

entries.definition: a short loud sound made by hard things hitting each other
entries.definitionCN: 硬物相撞发出的短促响声

entries.definition: a light ringing sound made by glass or metal
entries.definitionCN: 玻璃或金属相碰的清脆声

entries.definition: a small group of people who keep others out
entries.definitionCN: 排斥外人的小圈子

entries.definition: to hit something lightly and quickly
entries.definitionCN: 轻而快地敲一下

entries.definition: to push something firmly with a finger or hand
entries.definitionCN: 用手指或手掌用力按

entries.definition: the soft regular sound of a clock
entries.definitionCN: 钟表规律而轻柔的声响

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the snap of a latch, the mouse button and the moment an idea falls into place.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从门闩的脆响、鼠标按键和想法突然归位入手。

normal.en: Say the word aloud once and you have already made the sound it names.
normal.cn: 把这个词大声念一遍，你其实已经发出了它所命名的声音。

normal.en: The word is one syllable, as short as the noise itself.
normal.cn: 这个词只有一个音节，短得就像那声脆响。

normal.en: A latch clicks, a switch clicks, a mouse button clicks.
normal.cn: 门闩会咔一声，开关会咔一声，鼠标键也会咔一声。

normal.en: When an idea clicks, it locks into place like a latch.
normal.cn: 当想法一下子通了，它就像门闩一样扣进位置。

normal.en: Double-click puts two snaps together, so the ending joins with a hyphen.
normal.cn: double-click 把两次脆响并在一起，中间用连字符相连。

abstract.en: Picture a dark hallway and a latch snapping shut behind you.
abstract.cn: 想象一条昏暗的走廊，身后的门闩咔一声扣上。

abstract.en: Picture a finger resting on a mouse, one soft snap, then a page appears.
abstract.cn: 想象手指搭在鼠标上，轻轻一响，页面就出现了。

abstract.en: Picture a student who frowns, then smiles as the rule locks into place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个学生先皱眉，随后规则归位，他笑了。

examples.en: Click the link and the page will open in a new window.
examples.cn: 点击这个链接，页面会在新窗口打开。

examples.en: She heard the click of the latch and knew he was home.
examples.cn: 她听到门闩的咔嗒声，就知道他回来了。

examples.en: The rule finally clicked when the teacher drew a diagram.
examples.cn: 老师画了一张图，那条规则才终于让她明白了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 click 记成鼠标那一下脆响：手指一按，屏幕立刻回应。

root: 拟声词，模仿锁扣、开关合拢时的短促声响，二十世纪后用来指鼠标按键。

sensesIntro.en: From a small sound to a mouse action, and then to a mind that suddenly understands.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一声轻响，到鼠标动作，再到头脑突然明白。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger on a mouse button, one soft snap.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指按住鼠标键，发出轻轻一声脆响。

branches.en: A mouse button press borrows the name of its own sound.
branches.cn: 鼠标按键的动作借用了自己发出的声音之名。

branches.en: Locks, switches and heels all make this short snap.
branches.cn: 锁、开关和鞋跟都会发出这种短促的声响。

branches.en: A thought snaps into place like a latch closing.
branches.cn: 一个念头像门闩合上那样咔一下归位。

branches.en: One word covers the sound and the action that produces it.
branches.cn: 同一个词既指声音，也指发出声音的动作。

branches.en: The sharp snap became a picture for sudden understanding.
branches.cn: 清脆的一响成了突然领悟的形象说法。

intro.en: The word is too short to take prefixes, so its family grows by compounding and by common endings.
intro.cn: 这个词太短，无法再加前缀，家族靠复合与常见词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the base itself imitates a sound.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，词基本身就是拟声。

items.meaning: presses a mouse button or makes a small sound
items.example: He clicks the same icon every morning.
items.exampleCN: 他每天早上都点同一个图标。

items.meaning: pressed a button or made a small sound
items.example: She clicked the wrong link by mistake.

items.meaning: the act or repeated sound of a click
items.meaningCN: 点击的动作；连续的轻响
items.example: The clicking of the keyboard filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 键盘的咔嗒声充满了房间。

items.meaning: able to be clicked with a mouse
items.example: Every button on the page is clickable.
items.exampleCN: 页面上的每个按钮都可以点击。

items.meaning: a small device used to change channels
items.example: She changed the channel with a clicker.

items.meaning: to press a mouse button twice quickly
items.example: Double-click the folder to open it.
items.exampleCN: 双击这个文件夹把它打开。

items.meaning: to press the right button of a mouse
items.example: Right-click the file and choose copy.
items.exampleCN: 右键点击该文件并选择复制。

items.meaning: a title written only to attract clicks
items.exampleCN: 那个标题纯粹是在骗点击。

definition_zh: 客户；委托人；客户端
definition_en: a person or company that pays for goods or services, a person who uses a professional service, or a computer that requests data from a server
core_image: 会客室里等着谈生意的那位老主顾
scene: 律师事务所的沙发上坐着一位等了很久的先生。The lawyer met her client at nine in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 client 指「委托人」（第 2 个义项：接受专业人士服务的人）；句意是律师早上九点会见了她的委托人。

senses.title: A paying customer
senses.definition: a person or company that buys goods or services from a business
senses.definitionCN: 向商家购买商品或服务的个人或公司
senses.example: The firm lost its biggest client last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司去年失去了最大的客户。
senses.why: A client is someone who leans on a business for what he needs, so the word suits a steady business relationship.
senses.whyCN: 客户是依靠商家获得所需之物的人，所以这个词适合表示稳定的商业关系。

senses.title: A user of professional services
senses.definition: a person who pays a lawyer, designer or other professional for advice or work
senses.definitionCN: 付钱请律师、设计师等专业人士提供意见或工作的人
senses.example: The architect showed the client three designs.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师给委托人看了三份设计。
senses.why: Professionals serve one named person rather than a crowd, and that person is called a client.
senses.whyCN: 专业人士服务的是一位具名的人而不是人群，这个人就叫委托人。

senses.title: A computer that requests data
senses.definition: a computer or program that asks a server for data or services
senses.definitionCN: 向服务器请求数据或服务的计算机或程序
senses.example: The client sends a request and waits for the reply.
senses.exampleCN: 客户端发出请求，然后等待回复。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word because the small machine also depends on a larger provider.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用这个词，因为小机器同样依赖更大的服务方。

intro.en: Client comes from a Latin verb meaning to lean, not from any word for money.
intro.cn: client 出自拉丁语中表示倚靠的动词，与金钱毫无关系。

items.en: The family of clinare described leaning or bending.
items.cn: clinare 这一词族表示倾斜或倚靠。

items.en: Cliens named a follower who leaned on a patron for protection.
items.cn: cliens 指依靠庇护者保护的随从。

items.en: The word passed through French into legal language.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入法律用语。

items.en: Client first meant a person under another man's protection.
items.cn: client 最初指受他人保护的人。

items.en: Commerce widened it to any paying customer, and computing added the client machine.
items.cn: 商业把它扩展为任何付钱的顾客，计算机又添上客户端之义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that echo the spelling of client, while the meaning group names people who buy or use services.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写与 client 相近的词，近义组列出购买或使用服务的人。

entries.definition: a place where people go for medical advice or treatment
entries.definitionCN: 人们去看病或咨询的诊所

entries.definition: all the clients of a business or a professional person
entries.definitionCN: 一家企业或一位专业人士的全部客户

entries.definition: to hold on to something tightly
entries.definitionCN: 紧紧抓住某物

entries.definition: a person who buys goods or services from a shop
entries.definitionCN: 在商店购买商品或服务的人

entries.definition: a person who buys and uses goods and services
entries.definitionCN: 购买并使用商品和服务的人

entries.definition: a person who regularly uses a shop, hotel or theatre
entries.definitionCN: 经常光顾某商店、旅馆或剧院的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the leaning root, the waiting room and the difference between a client and a customer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从倚靠词根、会客室以及客户与顾客的区别入手。

normal.en: Client and customer both buy, but a client usually buys advice or a service.
normal.cn: client 与 customer 都买东西，但 client 通常买的是建议或服务。

normal.en: The Latin cliens was a follower who leaned on a patron.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 cliens 是依靠庇护者的随从。

normal.en: A lawyer has clients, while a supermarket has customers.
normal.cn: 律师有委托人，超市有顾客。

normal.en: The noun clientele keeps the same stem and means the whole group of clients.
normal.cn: 名词 clientele 词干相同，指全部客户。

normal.en: In computing the client asks and the server answers.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，客户端发问，服务器作答。

abstract.en: Picture a man in a coat waiting on a leather sofa with a folder on his knee.
abstract.cn: 想象一位穿外套的先生坐在皮沙发上，膝上放着文件夹。

abstract.en: Picture two hands, one leaning on the other for support.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手，一只手倚着另一只手支撑自己。

abstract.en: Picture a small laptop asking a huge grey server for a file.
abstract.cn: 想象一台小笔记本向巨大的灰色服务器索取文件。

examples.en: The designer sent the client a revised plan.
examples.cn: 设计师把修改后的方案发给了委托人。

examples.en: This bank treats every client as a long-term partner.
examples.cn: 这家银行把每位客户都当作长期伙伴。

examples.en: The client software updates itself once a week.
examples.cn: 客户端软件每周自动更新一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 client 想成「倚靠」你的人：他倚赖你的服务，你倚赖他的订单。

root: 源自拉丁语 cliens（依附者），出自表示倾斜、倚靠的词族，本义是依靠庇护者的人。

sensesIntro.en: From a dependent follower to a paying customer, then to the machine that asks a server.
sensesIntro.cn: 从依附的随从，到付钱的客户，再到向服务器发请求的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person leaning on a stronger partner for support.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人倚靠着更强的一方获取支撑。

branches.en: A steady buyer leans on a business, and the business keeps him.
branches.cn: 稳定的买家倚赖商家，商家也留住他。

branches.en: Professional work creates a named person who pays for advice.
branches.cn: 专业工作产生了一位为意见付费的具名之人。

branches.en: Software copies the pattern: the small side asks, the big side answers.
branches.cn: 软件复制了这个模式：小的一方发问，大的一方作答。

branches.en: Both senses keep one idea, a person served rather than a crowd.
branches.cn: 两个义项共有一个意思：被服务的是个人而非人群。

branches.en: Both use the word for the dependent side of a relationship.
branches.cn: 两者都用这个词指关系中的依赖方。

intro.en: The stem client carries the family, and most relatives simply add a suffix or join another word.
intro.cn: 词干 client 撑起整个家族，多数亲属词只是加后缀或与另一词复合。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin cliens, the dependent follower who leaned on a patron.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 cliens，即倚靠庇护者的依附者。

items.meaning: more than one customer or dependent person
items.example: The studio serves clients in three cities.
items.exampleCN: 这家工作室为三个城市的客户服务。

items.meaning: the whole group of clients of a business
items.example: The cafe has a young clientele.
items.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆的顾客以年轻人为主。

items.example: The new office opened clientless but hopeful.
items.exampleCN: 新办公室开业时没有客户，却满怀希望。

items.meaning: using one machine to ask and another to answer
items.example: The system follows a client-server model.
items.exampleCN: 该系统采用客户服务器模式。

items.meaning: all the customers a business can rely on
items.example: The merger doubled the client base.
items.exampleCN: 合并使客户基础扩大了一倍。

items.example: She moved into a client-facing role.
items.exampleCN: 她转到了一线面对客户的岗位。

items.example: The team keeps a client-focused habit.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队保持着以客户为中心的习惯。

items.meaning: the state of being a client
items.exampleCN: 客户身份带来定期的报告。

latinEntries.meaning: a follower who depends on a patron
latinEntries.example: Cliens gave English the word client.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cliens 给英语带来了 client 一词。

latinEntries.example: Clinare stands behind the image of leaning.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clinare 是「倚靠」这一意象的来源。

definition_zh: 客户群；顾客总称；（律师等的）委托人群体
definition_en: the body of clients or customers that a business, professional or institution serves
core_image: 一家小店的门口，几张熟悉的面孔按同样的顺序在同一个时间出现
scene: 小店门口，几张熟悉的面孔在同一个时间按同样的顺序出现。The clientele of the small hotel returns every August.
sceneCN: 小店门口，几张熟悉的面孔在同一个时间按同样的顺序出现；句中的这个词指「某机构所服务的顾客总体」（第 1 个义项：把许多客户当作一个整体来看的集合）。图中可辨识物件：店门、几张熟悉的面孔、固定的时刻、门牌、登记簿。

pos.zh: 客户群；顾客总称（集合名词，不可数）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多类客户群）

derivatives.zh: 委托关系；全体委托人群

senses.title: The whole body of customers
senses.definition: the body of clients or customers that a business, professional or institution serves
senses.definitionCN: 某个商家、专业人士或机构所服务的客户总体
senses.example: The clientele of the small hotel returns every August.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小旅馆的客源每年八月都会回来。
senses.why: The Latin noun named the whole group of dependants, not one dependant, so English took it as a collective.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词指的是依附者的整体，而不是某一个依附者，所以英语把它当作集合名词接收。

senses.title: The clients of a professional
senses.titleCN: 律师、会计师等的委托人群
senses.definition: the people or firms who pay a professional for advice or representation
senses.definitionCN: 为获得建议或代理而向专业人士付钱的人或公司
senses.example: His clientele is mostly small family firms.
senses.exampleCN: 他的委托人大多是小型家族企业。
senses.why: A professional's practice is measured by the group of people who rely on him, and that group is the clientele.
senses.whyCN: 一位专业人士的业务，是用依赖他的那群人来衡量的，而那群人就是 clientele。

senses.title: The trade of a restaurant or hotel
senses.definition: the customers who regularly use a place of hospitality
senses.definitionCN: 经常光顾某家餐饮或住宿场所的顾客
senses.example: The restaurant changed its clientele when it moved uptown.
senses.exampleCN: 餐厅搬到上城后，客源换了。
senses.why: A place has a character, and its clientele is the group that character attracts.
senses.whyCN: 一个场所自有一种性格，而它的 clientele 就是被这种性格吸引来的那群人。

senses.title: A group of habitual returners
senses.definition: the customers who come back again and again, seen as a group
senses.definitionCN: 反复回来的那些顾客，被当作一个群体来看
senses.example: Decades of work built a clientele that never moved away.
senses.exampleCN: 几十年的经营养出了一群从不离开的常客。
senses.why: Collective naming hides the individual: what matters is the pattern of return, not any one person.
senses.whyCN: 集合命名抹掉了个人：要紧的是「回来」这个模式，而不是任何一个人。

senses.title: A wealthy or select group
senses.definition: a clientele of high income or high status, often used as a selling point
senses.definitionCN: 收入高或身份高的客源，常用作卖点
senses.example: The jeweller's clientele includes three royal families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家珠宝店的客户里有三个王室。
senses.why: When a group is named collectively, it can be graded, and the grade becomes part of the shop's image.
senses.whyCN: 一群人被集合命名之后就可以被分级，而这个等级又成了店铺形象的一部分。

senses.title: The customer base a firm depends on
senses.definition: the total group whose custom keeps a business going
senses.definitionCN: 靠其惠顾维持生意的整个群体
senses.example: Losing half its clientele closed the clinic within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 失去一半客户后，这家诊所一年内就关门了。
senses.why: A collective noun can be treated as an asset: the group is what the business owns and can lose.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词可以被当作资产：这群人就是企业拥有、也可能失去的东西。

senses.title: The make-up of a customer group
senses.definition: the composition of a customer group by age, income, place or type
senses.definitionCN: 客户群体按年龄、收入、地域或类型形成的构成
senses.example: The bar's clientele is now two thirds students.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒吧的客源现在三分之二是学生。
senses.why: Once a group is counted, it can be broken into parts, and the parts describe the whole.
senses.whyCN: 一群人被计数之后就能拆成几部分，而这几部分又描述了整体。

senses.title: The patients or users of an institution
senses.definition: the group served by a clinic, a charity or a public institution
senses.definitionCN: 由诊所、慈善机构或公共机构所服务的那群人
senses.example: The clinic's clientele has grown older every year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所的就诊人群逐年变老。
senses.why: Service institutions also have dependants, and the old Latin word fits them as well as shops.
senses.whyCN: 服务机构同样有依附者，这个古老的拉丁词用在它们身上和用在商店身上一样合适。

intro.en: Clientele is the collective of client: Latin clientela, the whole body of dependants, borrowed through French.
intro.cn: clientele 是 client 的集合形式：拉丁 clientela 指依附者的整体，经法语借入英语。

items.en: Client comes from cliens, the present participle of cluere 'to hear, to listen, to obey'. The deeper origin of cluere is uncertain; it is generally considered related to a reconstructed root for hearing.
items.cn: client 出自 cliens，即 cluere「听、听从、服从」的现在分词。cluere 的更早来源不确定，一般认为与一个重构的「听」词根相关。

items.en: In Roman society a cliens was a dependent who owed loyalty and services to a patron, and who in return received protection and support. The plural is clientes.
items.cn: 在罗马社会，cliens 是依附于庇护人的从属者，对庇护人负有忠诚与服务之责，作为回报获得保护与支持。复数是 clientes。

items.en: Clientela named the whole condition and body of such dependants, the patronage relationship and the group itself.
items.cn: clientela 指这些依附者的整体状况与群体，也指庇护关系本身。

items.en: French clientèle kept the collective sense and passed it into English in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 clientèle 保留了集合义，并在十八世纪把它传入英语。

items.en: English applied the word to the customers of a shop or a hotel, so that a group of buyers inherited the tone of dependants.
items.cn: 英语把这个词用于商店或旅馆的顾客，于是一群买家继承了「依附者」的语气。

items.en: The word now names a customer group as an asset or a market segment, and it survives in political science as clientelism.
items.cn: 这个词如今把客户群当作资产或市场细分来命名，并在政治学里以 clientelism（庇护主义）的形式留存。

note.en: Group one shares the client root; group two names related collections of buyers.
note.cn: 第一组共享 client 词根；第二组是相关的买家集合。

entries.definition: One customer or principal. Clientele is the whole group, so it cannot be counted with numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 单个客户或委托人。clientele 是整群，所以不能用数字直接数。

entries.definition: The state of being a client, or the relation of dependence; it names the bond rather than the group.
entries.definitionCN: 作为客户的身份，或依附关系；它命名的是那层纽带，而不是群体。

entries.definition: A political system that trades favours for loyalty; it shares the root but belongs to politics, not retail.
