entries.definitionCN: 以恩惠换取忠诚的政治体制；共享词根，但属于政治而非零售。

entries.definition: The possessive form, as in the clientele's tastes. It is a grammar form, not a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 所有格形式，如 clientele's tastes。它是语法形式，不是另一个词。

entries.definition: The countable business phrase for the whole set of buyers; clientele is the same idea in older, more formal dress.
entries.definitionCN: 商业里指全部买家的可数说法；clientele 是同一想法的更古老、更正式的说法。

entries.definition: Individual buyers counted one by one; clientele treats them as one body.
entries.definitionCN: 一个一个数的个体买家；clientele 把他们当作一个整体。

entries.definition: A group that follows a person, brand or programme; it stresses devotion rather than paying.
entries.definitionCN: 追随某人、品牌或节目的一群人；强调忠诚，而非付钱。

entries.definition: The support a patron gives, or the custom of patrons as a body; it stresses the giving side.
entries.definitionCN: 庇护者给予的支持，或庇护者全体的惠顾；强调给予的一方。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: one Latin collective noun, one French spelling, one clear grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：一个拉丁集合名词、一个法语拼写、一条清楚的语法。

normal.en: client + -ele, from Latin clientela: the group, not the one.
normal.cn: client 加 -ele，出自拉丁 clientela：指群体，不指单个。

normal.en: The client root means 'one who listens and obeys', and a clientele is a whole body of such listeners.
normal.cn: client 词根意为「听从、服从的人」，而 clientele 是这样一群人的整体。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the group: a loyal clientele, a wealthy clientele, build a clientele.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示「群」：忠实的客户群、富裕的客户群、建立客户群。

normal.en: French clientèle explains the spelling: -èle, not the English -el.
normal.cn: 法语 clientèle 解释了拼写：是 -èle，不是英语的 -el。

normal.en: The political cousin clientelism keeps the same dependant picture.
normal.cn: 政治上的近亲 clientelism 保留了同一幅「依附」画面。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at one door where every face is familiar: the queue is the clientele.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门前排队，每张脸都熟悉：这支队伍就是 clientele。

abstract.en: A client is a thread; the clientele is the cloth woven from those threads.
abstract.cn: 一个 client 是一根线；clientele 是用这些线织成的布。

abstract.en: Because it is cloth, it can be measured, graded, lost and replaced.
abstract.cn: 正因为它是布，它可以被衡量、分级、失去、替换。

examples.en: The bookshop built its clientele through forty years of school orders.
examples.cn: 这家书店靠四十年的学校订单建立了客户群。

examples.en: A younger clientele now fills the bar on weeknights.
examples.cn: 如今工作日的晚上，酒吧里坐满更年轻的客源。

examples.en: The firm's clientele includes several city governments.
examples.cn: 这家公司的客户里有好几个市政府。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克利恩-泰尔」——克利恩们一排排站在泰尔（柜台）前，就是一群人 → clientele 客户群

root: 法语 clientèle，出自拉丁 clientela「依附者群体」；其词根 cliens 出自动词 cluere「听、听从」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all look at buyers as one body: a shop's trade, a professional's dependants, a hotel's regulars, a loyal circle, a select circle, an asset, a structure and an institution's served group.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把买家当作一个整体来看：一家商店的客源、一位专业人士的委托人、一家旅馆的常客、一个忠实圈子、一个高端圈子、一项资产、一种结构，以及一个机构的受助群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a familiar queue at one door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门前一支熟悉的面孔排成的队。

branches.en: GROUP AND ASSET: the same body can be described as a set of people or as what a business owns.
branches.cn: 群体与资产：同一群人既可被描述为一群人，也可被描述为企业拥有的东西。

branches.en: DEPENDANTS: the Roman follower survives in the professional's clients and in the institution's patients.
branches.cn: 依附者：罗马的从属者活在专业人士的委托人与机构的就诊者身上。

branches.en: PLACE: a restaurant's character selects its trade.
branches.cn: 场所：一家餐厅的性格筛出了它的客源。

branches.en: RETURN: loyalty exists only as repetition.
branches.cn: 回头：忠诚只以重复的形式存在。

branches.en: GRADE AND COMPOSITION: a collective can be valued and also broken into parts.
branches.cn: 等级与构成：一个集合体既能被估值，也能被拆成几部分。

intro.en: Clientele is the Latin collective of client, borrowed whole through French, so it adds no English suffix of its own.
intro.cn: clientele 是 client 的拉丁集合形式，整体经法语借入，因此自身不带英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cliens 'listener, dependant' and clientela 'body of dependants' both come from cluere 'to hear, obey'; the deeper origin of cluere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cliens「听从者、依附者」与 clientela「依附者群体」都出自 cluere「听、服从」；cluere 的更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: one who pays for a service

items.example: The clientele stayed loyal for decades.
items.exampleCN: 客户群几十年保持忠诚。

items.example: Clientage bound him to one patron.
items.exampleCN: 依附关系把他绑在一位庇护人身上。

items.meaningCN: 以恩惠交换忠诚的政治
items.exampleCN: 庇护主义削弱了文官体系。

items.example: The verb describes a follower's duty.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述跟随者的义务。

items.example: A cliens owed service to a patron.
items.exampleCN: 依附者对庇护人负有服务之责。

items.meaning: the customers a firm relies on
items.example: The client base grew by a third.
items.exampleCN: 客户基础增长了三分之一。

definition_zh: 气候；氛围；形势
definition_en: the usual weather conditions of a place over a long period, or the general mood and conditions in a group or period
core_image: 同一片天空下年年重复的雨与晴
scene: 老人翻着几十年的农事笔记，记下每年第一场雨的日子。The mild climate here suits tea and oranges.
sceneCN: 这里 climate 指「气候」（第 1 个义项：一个地方长期的天气状况）；句意是这里温和的气候适合种茶和柑橘。

senses.title: Long-term weather of a place
senses.definition: the usual weather conditions of a region over many years
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区多年间反复出现的天气状况
senses.example: The island has a warm climate and little snow.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛气候温暖，很少下雪。
senses.why: Greek geographers divided the world into belts by the angle of the sun, and each belt became a climate.
senses.whyCN: 希腊地理学家按日照角度把世界分成带，每一条带就叫一个气候区。

senses.title: The mood of a group
senses.definition: the general feeling or attitude among a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 一群人当中普遍的情绪或态度
senses.example: A climate of trust made the talks easier.
senses.exampleCN: 信任的氛围让谈判顺利了许多。
senses.why: Weather surrounds people and shapes their day, and so does a shared mood, which borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 天气包围并影响人的一天，共同的氛围也是如此，于是借用了同一个词。

senses.title: Conditions affecting decisions
senses.definition: the economic or political conditions that affect how people act
senses.definitionCN: 影响人们行动方式的经济或政治条件
senses.example: Few firms hire in such a poor climate.
senses.exampleCN: 在如此糟糕的形势下，很少有公司招人。
senses.why: Business writers needed a word for the surrounding conditions, and the weather word was ready.
senses.whyCN: 商业作者需要一个词表示周围的条件，天气词正好现成可用。

intro.en: Climate began as a Greek word for a slope, because the sun's angle decides how warm a region is.
intro.cn: climate 最初是希腊语中表示斜坡的词，因为日照角度决定了一个地区的冷暖。

items.en: Klima meant a slope or a zone of the earth.
items.cn: klima 指斜坡或地球上的一条地带。

items.en: Geographers used it for bands of the world marked by sun and slope.
items.cn: 地理学家用它指按日照与坡度划分的地带。

items.en: Clima kept the sense of a zone of the earth.
items.cn: clima 保留了地球地带的意思。

items.en: The word entered French as climat.
items.cn: 这个词以 climat 的形式进入法语。

items.en: English first used it for a region and its weather.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指一个地区及其天气。

items.en: The word widened to the mood of a group and the state of business.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到群体氛围与商业形势。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in spelling, while the meaning group covers weather, surroundings and shared mood.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词，近义组涵盖天气、环境与共同情绪。

entries.definition: to move upward using hands and feet
entries.definitionCN: 手脚并用地向上移动

entries.definition: the most exciting or important point of a story
entries.definitionCN: 故事中最激动人心或最重要的时刻

entries.definition: an old poetic word for a region and its weather
entries.definitionCN: 古诗文中指某个地区及其天气

entries.definition: the condition of the air on a particular day
entries.definitionCN: 某一天空气的具体状况

entries.definition: the feeling that a place or event gives people
entries.definitionCN: 某个地方或事件给人的感觉

entries.definition: the conditions and surroundings in which people live
entries.definitionCN: 人们生活所处的条件与周围情况

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the sun's angle, the long record of weather and the mood of a meeting room.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从日照角度、长期天气记录和会议室气氛入手。

normal.en: Climate and climb share a start: both look up at the sky.
normal.cn: climate 与 climb 开头相同：两者都抬头看天。

normal.en: Weather is today; climate is the average of many years.
normal.cn: weather 是今天，climate 是许多年的平均。

normal.en: The Greek klima meant a slope, because slope decides how much sun a place gets.
normal.cn: 希腊语 klima 意为斜坡，因为坡度决定一个地方得到多少阳光。

normal.en: The same word covers the room as well as the sky: a climate of trust.
normal.cn: 同一个词既能说天空，也能说房间：信任的氛围。

normal.en: Climatic keeps the adjective, climatology keeps the science.
normal.cn: climatic 是形容词，climatology 是这门学科。

abstract.en: Picture a globe marked with belts, hot at the middle and cold at the poles.
abstract.cn: 想象一个划成条带的地球，中间炎热，两极寒冷。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer's notebook full of rain dates across forty years.
abstract.cn: 想象一本农家笔记，记满四十年间的降雨日期。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet meeting room where everyone nods before speaking.
abstract.cn: 想象一间安静的会议室，人人发言前都先点头。

examples.en: The climate here is too dry for rice.
examples.cn: 这里的气候太干燥，不适合种稻。

examples.en: Climate change is reshaping the coast.
examples.cn: 气候变化正在改变海岸的面貌。

examples.en: The company expanded in a favourable economic climate.
examples.cn: 这家公司在有利的经济形势下扩张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 climate 记成「斜坡上的天气」：坡向哪儿，阳光就怎么照，一方水土便有了脾气。

root: 源自希腊语 klima（斜坡、地带），经拉丁语 clima 与法语 climat 进入英语，本义是按日照划分的地带。

sensesIntro.en: From a band of the earth to the weather of a place, then to the mood around people and the state of trade.
sensesIntro.cn: 从地球上的地带，到一个地方的天气，再到人群氛围与商业形势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slope of land under a particular angle of sun.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片土地在特定日照角度下形成的斜坡。

branches.en: The physical sense is the long weather record of one region.
branches.cn: 实义是一个地区长期的天气记录。

branches.en: A shared feeling wraps a group the way weather wraps a town.
branches.cn: 共同的感受笼罩一个群体，就像天气笼罩一座城。

branches.en: Economic conditions become a climate that firms must read.
branches.cn: 经济条件成了一种企业必须判读的气候。

branches.en: Both senses describe surroundings that people cannot easily change.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述人们不易改变的环境。

branches.en: Mood and market conditions are both the air a decision is made in.
branches.cn: 氛围与市场条件都是做决定时所处的空气。

intro.en: The stem climat carries the family, with adjective, adverb and scientific endings added.
intro.cn: 词干 climat 撑起家族，再添加形容词、副词与学科词尾。

latinIntro.en: The base is Greek klima, a slope, which Latin took over as clima.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是希腊语 klima（斜坡），拉丁语把它接收为 clima。

items.meaning: more than one pattern of regional weather
items.example: The book compares climates on three continents.
items.exampleCN: 这本书比较了三大洲的气候。

items.example: Climatic zones shift as the earth warms.
items.exampleCN: 随着地球变暖，气候带发生移动。

items.example: The two ports are climatically similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两个港口在气候上相似。

items.example: She studied climatology for six years.
A climatologist explained the rainfall data.
items.exampleCN: 一位气候学家解释了降雨数据。

items.meaning: the climate of one small area
items.example: The valley has its own microclimate.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷有自己的小气候。

items.meaning: not harmful to the global climate
items.exampleCN: 他们选择了对气候友好的供暖方式。

items.meaning: a long-term shift in global weather patterns
items.example: Climate change is a global issue.
items.exampleCN: 气候变化是一个全球性问题。

latinEntries.meaning: a zone or belt of the earth
latinEntries.example: Clima passed into French and then English.

definition_zh: 气候的；与一个地区长期天气状况有关的
definition_en: relating to the long-term weather conditions of a region rather than to a single day's weather
core_image: 同一条山坡上，几十年的温度曲线被压成一条缓慢起伏的平滑长线
scene: 山谷里的气象站保存了几十年的温度与降水记录。Long-term records show a climatic shift toward warmer winters.
sceneCN: 这里 climatic 指「与长期气候状况有关的」（第 1 个义项：气候的）；句意为长期记录显示气候正朝更暖的冬季偏移。图中可辨识物件：百叶箱、记录纸、温度曲线、山谷。

pos.zh: 由气候造成的；气候性的

senses.title: Relating to climate
senses.definition: relating to the weather conditions that a region has over many years
senses.definitionCN: 与一个地区多年来的天气状况有关
senses.example: Climatic conditions decide which crops ripen in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 气候条件决定这个山谷里哪些作物能够成熟。
senses.why: the adjective simply attaches the noun climate to whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词「气候」挂到它所描述的事物上。

senses.title: Caused by climate
senses.definition: produced or driven by long-term weather patterns rather than by a single event
senses.definitionCN: 由长期天气模式造成，而非由单次事件造成
senses.example: The canyon's shape is partly a climatic effect of dry centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这条峡谷的形态部分是数百年干旱造成的气候性结果。
senses.why: once climate names a cause, the adjective can mark an effect that follows from it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦气候被当作原因，这个形容词就能标示由它产生的后果。

senses.title: Of a climatic zone
senses.definition: relating to one of the broad belts into which the earth is divided by climate
senses.definitionCN: 与按气候把地球划分成的某个大带有关
senses.example: The map colours each climatic zone a different shade.
senses.exampleCN: 地图用不同深浅的颜色标出每一个气候带。
senses.why: the oldest sense of the root is a belt or zone, so the adjective still marks those belts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根最早的意思就是「带、区域」，因此这个形容词仍用来标示这些带。

senses.title: Of climate records
senses.definition: relating to the measured series of temperature, rainfall and other weather data
senses.definitionCN: 与温度、降水等长期观测数据序列有关
senses.example: Climatic records from the station go back to the nineteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个台站的气候记录可追溯到十九世纪。
senses.why: data are called climatic when they describe climate rather than a day's weather.
senses.whyCN: 当数据描述的是气候而非某一天的天气时，就被称作气候数据。

senses.title: Of biological adaptation
senses.definition: relating to the adjustments by which living things cope with a particular climate
senses.definitionCN: 与生物为适应特定气候而做出的调整有关
senses.example: Thick fur is a climatic adaptation found in many mountain mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 厚毛是许多山地哺乳动物身上可见的一种气候适应。
senses.why: ecology borrowed the adjective to label traits shaped by long-term weather.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个形容词，用来标示被长期天气塑造的性状。

senses.title: Of extremes
senses.definition: relating to unusually severe weather that a climate makes more or less likely
senses.definitionCN: 与某种气候使之更易或更不易发生的异常剧烈天气有关
senses.example: Climatic extremes such as heat waves now appear in the risk models.
senses.exampleCN: 热浪这类极端气候事件如今进入了风险模型。
senses.why: the adjective shifts from typical conditions to the rare events those conditions produce.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从典型状况转指这些状况所催生的罕见事件。

senses.title: Of variability
senses.definition: relating to how much climate varies from year to year or decade to decade
senses.definitionCN: 与气候在年际或年代际间的变化幅度有关
senses.example: Climatic variability makes a single dry year hard to interpret.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变率使得单独一个干旱年份难以解读。
senses.why: a climate is not a constant, and the adjective covers its range of change.
senses.whyCN: 气候并非常量，这个形容词涵盖它的变化幅度。

senses.title: Of projections and models
senses.definition: relating to calculated future climates produced by computer models
senses.definitionCN: 与计算机模式算出的未来气候有关
senses.example: Climatic projections disagree mainly about the next fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 气候预估的分歧主要集中在未来五十年。
senses.why: the newest sense comes from modelling, where the adjective marks a computed rather than observed climate.
senses.whyCN: 最新的义项来自建模，此时这个形容词标示的是算出的而非观测到的气候。

intro.en: Climatic is climate plus the Latin-derived suffix -ic, and climate goes back through Latin and Greek to a word for a slope or a zone. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: climatic 是 climate 加拉丁来源的后缀 -ic；climate 则经拉丁语与希腊语追溯到表示「斜坡、地带」的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek klima meant 'slope, inclination', then 'zone of the earth', because the inhabited zones were pictured as bands tilted from the equator toward the poles. It comes from klimein 'to lean'.
items.cn: 希腊 klima 意为「斜坡、倾斜」，后指「地带」，因为当时把人居地带想象成从赤道向两极倾斜的条带。它出自 klimein「倾斜」。

items.en: Latin clima, climat- took the Greek word into geographical writing, where it named a belt of the earth fixed by latitude.
items.cn: 拉丁 clima（词干 climat-）把希腊词带入地理写作，用来指由纬度确定的地球条带。

items.en: Old French climat and Latin climat- gave English climate in the late fourteenth century, first as a geographical belt and later as the typical weather of a region.
items.cn: 古法语 climat 与拉丁词干 climat- 在十四世纪末带来英语 climate，最初指地理上的带，后来指一个地区的典型天气。

items.en: The adjective climatic was formed on climate with the suffix -ic in the nineteenth century, once climate had acquired its modern weather meaning.
items.cn: 形容词 climatic 在十九世纪由 climate 加后缀 -ic 构成，此时 climate 已获得现代天气义。

items.en: Climatic then spread into compounds such as climatic zone, climatic change and climatic data.
items.cn: climatic 随后扩展到气候带、气候变迁、气候资料等固定说法中。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first use of climatic is recorded, and it is usually placed in the nineteenth century; its formation from climate is transparent.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：climatic 的确切首见英语书证未被记录，通常放在十九世纪；它由 climate 构成，来路清楚。

note.en: Group one holds the word most often mistaken for climatic, plus near neighbours from different roots; group two holds adjectives that genuinely describe weather or climate.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易被误作 climatic 的词，以及来自不同词根的相邻词；第二组才是真正描述天气或气候的形容词。

entries.definition: From Greek klimax 'ladder' through climax: relating to the most intense point of a story or event. It has nothing to do with climate.
entries.definitionCN: 经 climax 来自希腊 klimax「梯子」：指故事或事件最紧张的高点。与气候无关。

entries.definition: From Greek klimaktēr 'rung of a ladder': a critical period or turning point, also used in physiology.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 klimaktēr「梯级」：指关键时期或转折点，也用于生理学。

entries.definition: A poetic shortening of climate, still used for a region and its weather; it shares the root but not the technical range.
entries.definitionCN: climate 的诗体缩略形式，仍指地区及其天气；词根相同，技术用法范围不同。

entries.definition: The descriptive mapping of climates, as opposed to climatology, which studies causes and processes.
entries.definitionCN: 对气候的描述性制图，与研究成因与过程的气候学相对。

entries.definition: Relating to weather and its observation; a single storm is meteorological, a shift over decades is climatic.
entries.definitionCN: 与天气及其观测有关；一场风暴是气象的，数十年的偏移才是气候的。

entries.definition: Relating to the whole surroundings, of which climate is one part; it is wider and less precise.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个周围环境有关，气候只是其中一部分；范围更宽，也更不精确。

entries.definition: Relating to the cycle of seasons within a year, not to multi-year climate.
entries.definitionCN: 与一年内的季节循环有关，而非多年气候。

entries.definition: A plain compound for anything caused by day-to-day weather; it lacks the long timescale of climatic.
entries.definitionCN: 指由日常天气造成的任何事情的朴素复合说法；缺少 climatic 的长时间尺度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek klima 'slope, zone' gives climate, and climate plus -ic gives climatic.
normal.cn: 希腊 klima「斜坡、地带」给出 climate，climate 加 -ic 得到 climatic。

normal.en: The family runs climate, climatic, climatically, climatology, climatologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 climate、climatic、climatically、climatology、climatologist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the two registers: climatic change and climatic zone.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分两种语域：气候变迁与气候带。

normal.en: The classic trap is climactic, which belongs to climax and means the peak of a story.
normal.cn: 经典陷阱是 climactic，它属于 climax，指故事的高潮。

normal.en: A climate is measured in decades; a weather report is measured in hours.
normal.cn: 气候以十年计，天气报告以小时计。

abstract.en: Picture a single smooth line drawn through thousands of jagged daily readings.
abstract.cn: 想象一条平滑的长线穿过成千上万个锯齿状的每日读数。

abstract.en: Picture a broad band of colour painted across a continent.
abstract.cn: 想象一整条宽色带横涂在大陆上。

abstract.en: Picture a slope so gentle that a whole life fits on it without a bump.
abstract.cn: 想象一道坡缓得能放下人的一生而不见一个凸起。

examples.en: Climatic zones shift slowly as the ocean currents change.
examples.cn: 随着洋流改变，气候带缓慢移动。

examples.en: The study separates climatic effects from human ones.
examples.cn: 这项研究把气候造成的影响与人为影响分开。

examples.en: Climatic data from the ice core cover ten thousand years.
examples.cn: 来自冰芯的气候资料覆盖一万年。

dict_mnemonic.text: climate 是「气候」，加 -ic 就成「气候的」；记住它不是 climactic（高潮的），两者只差一个字母却完全不同源

root: 希腊 klima「斜坡、地带」（出自 klimein「倾斜」）→ 拉丁 clima（词干 climat-）→ 英语 climate → climate + -ic → climatic；与 climax 来的 climactic 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one long timescale: the general adjective, then effects, belts, records, adaptations, extremes, variability and finally computed futures.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都沿着同一个长时间尺度展开：先是一般形容词，再是后果、地带、记录、适应、极端事件、变化幅度，最后是算出的未来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one smooth line drawn through thousands of jagged daily readings.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条平滑的线穿过成千上万个锯齿状的每日读数。

branches.en: THE PATTERN AND THE BELT: the adjective names a region's long-run weather and the broad zones drawn from it.
branches.cn: 模式与地带：这个形容词指一个地区的长期天气，以及据此画出的宽大地带。

branches.en: FROM CONDITION TO EVENT: a climate both shapes ordinary conditions and makes rare extremes more likely.
branches.cn: 从状况到事件：气候既塑造日常状况，也使罕见的极端事件更易发生。

branches.en: THE RECORD: measurement turns a pattern into a series that can be read.
branches.cn: 记录：测量把一种模式变成可读取的序列。

branches.en: THE RESPONSE: living things adjust to a climate, and the adjective labels those traits.
branches.cn: 回应：生物适应气候，这个形容词就标示这些性状。

branches.en: RANGE AND FORECAST: the pattern is never constant, and its future is now computed.
branches.cn: 幅度与预报：这种模式从不是常量，而它的未来如今由计算给出。

intro.en: Climatic is a noun plus a suffix, and both the noun and the suffix have long histories that also build many related words.
intro.cn: climatic 是一个名词加一个后缀，名词与后缀都有很长的历史，也各自构成许多相关词。

latinIntro.en: Greek klima and Latin clima give climate; the suffix -ic goes back to Greek -ikos through Latin -icus and marks a relation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 klima 与拉丁 clima 给出 climate；后缀 -ic 经拉丁 -icus 出自希腊 -ikos，表示某种关系。

items.example: The word began as a description of tilt.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初描述的是倾斜。
拉丁地理学列出七个地带。

items.meaning: the long-term weather of a region
items.example: The valley has a dry climate.
The two sites are climatically similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两个地点在气候上相似。
气候学比较的是十年，不是一天。

items.example: A climatologist read the ice core.
items.exampleCN: 一位气候学家解读了冰芯。

items.meaning: relating to a peak or climax
items.example: The climactic scene ends the film.
items.exampleCN: 高潮场景结束了这部电影。

definition_zh: 攀登；爬；上升
definition_en: to move upward using your hands and feet, to rise in amount or level, or an act of going up
core_image: 双手抓住岩缝一点点向上挪动
scene: 天还没亮，队伍已经在山脚系好鞋带。They plan to climb the north face before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 climb 指「攀登」（第 1 个义项：手脚并用向上移动）；句意是他们打算中午前攀上北壁。

senses.title: Go up with hands and feet
senses.definition: to move upward on a steep surface using your hands and feet
senses.definitionCN: 在陡峭的表面上手脚并用向上移动
senses.example: The children climbed the old oak tree.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们爬上了那棵老橡树。
senses.why: The old verb described effort against gravity, so it keeps the picture of hands and feet.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老的动词描述对抗重力的用力，因此保留着手脚并用的画面。

senses.title: Rise in amount or level
senses.definition: to increase gradually in number, price or temperature
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、价格或温度上逐步升高
senses.example: Fuel prices climbed again last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月燃料价格又上涨了。
senses.why: A rising line on a chart looks like a slope being climbed, so the verb moved to figures.
senses.whyCN: 图表上上扬的线像在爬坡，这个动词便迁移到了数字上。

senses.title: An upward journey
senses.definition: a journey or movement upward, often a long or hard one
senses.definitionCN: 向上的行程或移动，往往漫长而费力
senses.example: The last climb to the summit took four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 登顶的最后一段爬升花了四个小时。
senses.why: English often turns a verb into a noun, and the action then becomes a countable trip.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动词用作名词，动作便成了一次可数的行程。

intro.en: Climb is an Old English verb for going up with effort, and its silent b is a spelling habit.
intro.cn: climb 是表示费力向上的古英语动词，其中不发音的 b 是拼写习惯留下的。

items.en: Climban meant to go up with effort, usually with hands and feet.
items.cn: climban 指费力向上，通常手脚并用。

items.en: Related verbs in German and Dutch named the same effort.
items.cn: 德语和荷兰语中的相关动词表示同样的用力。

items.en: The final b often dropped out of ordinary speech.
items.cn: 在日常口语中，词尾的 b 常常脱落。

items.en: Writers restored the b, which has been silent ever since.
items.cn: 文人恢复了字母 b，此后它一直不发音。

items.en: Prices and numbers climb too, so no ladder is needed.
items.cn: 价格和数字也会 climb，所以不再需要梯子。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the shape of climb, while the meaning group names ways of going up.
note.cn: 形近组收与 climb 形近的词，近义组列出向上行进的说法。

entries.definition: an old poetic word for a region and its weather
entries.definitionCN: 古诗文中指地区及其天气

entries.definition: the most intense point of a story or event
entries.definitionCN: 故事或事件中最紧张的时刻

entries.definition: a person who climbs, or a plant that climbs
entries.definitionCN: 攀登者，或会攀爬的植物

entries.definition: to go up along a slope or a stair
entries.definitionCN: 沿斜坡或阶梯向上

entries.definition: to get on a horse or to go up something
entries.definitionCN: 骑上马，或登上某物

entries.definition: to climb a wall or a high rock with effort
entries.definitionCN: 费力地攀登墙壁或高岩

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the silent letter, the mountain path and the rising price line.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从不发音的字母、山道和上扬的价格线入手。

normal.en: The b in climb is silent, so say the word as if it were clime.
normal.cn: climb 里的 b 不发音，读起来就像 clime。

normal.en: Climb keeps the same shape as limb, and you climb with your limbs.
normal.cn: climb 与 limb 形状相近，而人正是用四肢攀登。

normal.en: A climb is up, never down, so the word always points to the summit.
normal.cn: climb 只向上不向下，所以这个词永远指向山顶。

normal.en: The climber adds -er, and the climbing adds -ing.
normal.cn: climber 加 -er 指人，climbing 加 -ing 指这项运动。

normal.en: Prices climb, hopes climb, and the temperature climbs in July.
normal.cn: 价格会爬升，希望会攀升，七月的温度也会上升。

abstract.en: Picture two dusty hands finding a crack in the rock.
abstract.cn: 想象两只沾满灰尘的手在岩壁上摸到一道裂缝。

abstract.en: Picture a line of climbers on a ridge before sunrise.
abstract.cn: 想象日出前山脊上一串登山者的身影。

abstract.en: Picture a price line on a screen going up step by step.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一条价格线一步一步往上走。

examples.en: We climbed for six hours before reaching the ridge.
examples.cn: 我们爬了六个小时才到达山脊。

examples.en: The cat climbed onto the roof and would not come down.
examples.cn: 那只猫爬上屋顶，怎么也不肯下来。

examples.en: Rents have climbed faster than wages in this city.
examples.cn: 在这座城市，房租涨得比工资快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 climb 想成「用四肢（limb）向上」：手抓脚蹬，一寸一寸往上挪。

root: 源自古英语 climban（费力向上），属日耳曼语族，本义是手脚并用地攀援。

sensesIntro.en: From hands on rock to a rising price, then back to the journey itself as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 从手抓岩石，到价格上涨，再回到作为名词的这段行程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands and feet pulling a body up a steep face.
core.cn: 核心意象：手脚把身体拉上一面陡坡。

branches.en: The physical sense keeps the old picture of effort and grip.
branches.cn: 实义保留了用力与抓握的古老画面。

branches.en: A rising figure on a chart is a slope to be climbed.
branches.cn: 图表上上升的数字就是一段待爬的坡。

branches.en: The trip itself becomes a countable noun with a beginning and an end.
branches.cn: 这段路程本身成了有始有终的可数名词。

branches.en: The verb and the noun describe the same upward movement.
branches.cn: 动词与名词描述的是同一种向上运动。

branches.en: Both use the idea of steady upward progress.
branches.cn: 两者都借助稳步向上的进程这一意象。

intro.en: The base verb grows a noun for the person, a noun for the sport and a few compounds.
intro.cn: 这个动词长出指人的名词、指运动的名词以及若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the root is the Old English verb climban.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，词根是古英语动词 climban。

items.meaning: goes up using hands and feet
items.example: She climbs the same hill every Sunday.
items.exampleCN: 她每个星期天都爬同一座小山。

items.example: They climbed the tower before dusk.
items.exampleCN: 他们在黄昏前爬上了那座塔。

items.meaning: the activity of going up rocks or mountains
items.example: Climbing demands strong fingers and calm nerves.
items.exampleCN: 攀岩需要有力的手指和镇定的神经。

items.meaning: a person or plant that climbs
items.example: The climber paused below the overhang.
items.exampleCN: 攀登者在岩檐下方停了一下。

items.example: The wall is low and easily climbable.
items.exampleCN: 那堵墙很低，容易爬上去。

items.meaning: the sport of climbing rock faces
items.example: Rock climbing is popular in this valley.
items.exampleCN: 攀岩在这条山谷很流行。

items.meaning: the activity of climbing high mountains
items.example: Mountain climbing takes weeks of planning.

items.meaning: to admit that you were wrong
items.example: The minister had to climb down over the plan.
items.exampleCN: 部长不得不就这项计划让步。

definition_zh: 诊所；门诊部；（短期的）讲习班
definition_en: a place where people receive medical treatment but do not stay overnight
core_image: 一张安静的诊疗床，医生坐在床边问诊
scene: 放学后，妈妈带弟弟去小区的门诊部看嗓子。The doctor at the clinic checked his throat quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 clinic 是「诊所；门诊部」（第 1 个义项：可以看病但不用住院的地方）；句意是诊所医生很快检查了他的喉咙。

derivatives.zh: 由 clinic  + suffix  -al 构成，义为「临床的；诊所的」
由 clinic  + suffix  -ician 构成，义为「临床医生」

senses.title: A place for medical treatment without staying overnight
senses.definition: a place where a doctor treats patients who do not stay there
senses.definitionCN: 医生为无需留宿的病人看病的地方
senses.example: The new clinic near the station opens at eight.
senses.exampleCN: 车站附近的新诊所八点开门。
senses.why: Doctors once taught at the bedside of patients, and the place where this happened became the clinic.
senses.whyCN: 医生早先在病人床边教学查房，这一地点便得名 clinic。

senses.title: A special medical service or course
senses.titleCN: 专科门诊；（学校的）健康服务
senses.definition: an organized medical service for one special problem
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一专门问题的医疗服务
senses.example: The school runs an eye clinic every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 学校每年春天开设眼科门诊。
senses.why: One problem, one room, one team: medicine splits big care into focused little units.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题、一间诊室、一组医生：医疗把大病区拆成聚焦的小单元。

senses.title: A short course of practical teaching
senses.definition: a short class where a skill is taught in practice
senses.definitionCN: 短期传授某项技能的实践课
senses.example: Uncle Wang teaches at a free basketball clinic on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 王叔叔周日在免费篮球训练营教球。
senses.why: Doctors' bedside lessons felt like coaching, so other sports borrowed the word for skill classes.
senses.whyCN: 医生的床边教学像示范训练，其他项目便借用这个词指技能班。

intro.en: Clinic begins with a bed: the whole word family grows from lying down.
intro.cn: clinic 始于一张床：整个词族都从「躺卧」生长出来。

items.en: Greek kline meant a bed or couch on which sick people lay.
items.cn: 希腊语 kline 指病人躺卧的床或长榻。

items.en: Latin clinicus described a doctor who visited patients at their beds.
items.cn: 拉丁语 clinicus 描述到病床边诊视的医生。

items.en: French clinique kept the bedside sense for medical teaching hospitals.
items.cn: 法语 clinique 保留了「床边教学医院」的含义。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the eighteenth century for bedside medical teaching.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入该词，指床边医学教学。

items.en: Later English used clinic for the building and then for short practical courses.
items.cn: 后来 clinic 又指诊所建筑，再引申为短期讲习班。

note.en: The first group collects the clinic word family; the second collects places that give care.
note.cn: 第一组收 clinic 词族，第二组收提供医疗照护的场所。

entries.definition: Relating to the treatment of patients.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「临床的」，由 clinic 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: A doctor who works directly with patients.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「临床医生」，由 clinic 加 -ician 构成。

entries.definition: To hold on tightly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「紧抓」，拼写与 clinic 开头相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: A large place for serious illness and overnight care.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「医院」，规模更大、可住院。

entries.definition: In British English, a doctor's office.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式英语义为「医生的诊室」。

entries.definition: A small room for sick students or workers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「医务室」，常在学校或工厂。

normalIntro.en: Remember clinic through its bed root and its family words.
normalIntro.cn: 通过「床」的词根与词族记忆 clinic。

normal.en: clinic comes from a Greek word for bed.
normal.cn: clinic 来自希腊语「床」。

normal.en: clinical means connected with treating patients.
normal.cn: clinical 意为「临床的」。

normal.en: clinician is the doctor in a clinic.
normal.cn: clinician 指诊所里的临床医生。

normal.en: A dental clinic cares for teeth.

normal.en: Sports teams hold clinics to teach skills.
normal.cn: 运动队用 clinic 开设技能班。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor pulling a chair beside a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象医生把椅子拉到床边坐下。

abstract.en: Hear the low murmur of questions and answers at the bedside.
abstract.cn: 听床边一问一答的低语。

abstract.en: Feel the calm order of a small, tidy consulting room.
abstract.cn: 感受小诊室里安静有序的气氛。

examples.en: Grandma goes to the clinic for her blood test every month.
examples.cn: 奶奶每个月去诊所验血。

examples.en: The sports clinic taught me how to pass the ball.
examples.cn: 训练营教会了我怎么传球。

examples.en: The clinic was quiet because the doctor was out on a call.
examples.cn: 诊所很安静，因为医生出诊去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克里尼克」——病人躺在「床」上，医生克勤克俭地护理，clinic 就是床边的小诊所。

root: 希腊语 kline（床）→ 拉丁语 clinicus（到床边诊视的医生）→ 法语 clinique → 十八世纪英语 clinic（床边教学）→ 现代英语「诊所」；派生词有 clinical（临床的）、clinician（临床医生）。

sensesIntro.en: Clinic grew from a bedside lesson to a treatment room and a training class.
sensesIntro.cn: clinic 从床边教学延伸到诊疗室，再到技能训练班。

core.cn: 核心意象：病床边医生的那把椅子

branches.en: The treatment room
branches.cn: 看病的场所

branches.en: One problem, one service
branches.cn: 针对单一问题的门诊

branches.cn: 短期技能班

branches.en: Everyday medical care
branches.cn: 日常医疗照护

intro.en: The bed root builds a whole medical family.
intro.cn: 「床」词根繁衍出整个医疗词族。

latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kline 与拉丁语 clinare 都出自「倚靠、躺卧」这同一个意象。

The polyclinic sees both eyes and teeth.

latinEntries.meaning: a doctor who treats patients at the bedside
to visit and examine the sick

definition_zh: 临床的；诊所的；冷静客观的；简朴无装饰的
definition_en: relating to the treatment of patients at the bedside, and by extension detached, analytical and plain
core_image: 医生俯身病床，只看症状和数字，不掺入自己的情绪
scene: 这组词中，A doctor reads a chart at the bedside and says: Let's keep this clinical — just the test results.
sceneCN: 这里 clinical 是「冷静客观的、只谈事实的」（第 5 个义项：像病历报告一样不带感情）；句意：我们临床一点，只看检验结果。画面里是病床、病历夹和监护仪。

pos.zh: 冷静客观的；不带感情的

derivatives.zh: 亚临床的；无明显症状的

senses.title: Bedside medicine: care given at the patient's bed
senses.titleCN: 临床的：在病人床边进行的医疗
senses.definition: relating to the observation and treatment of patients, especially at the bedside rather than in theory
senses.definitionCN: 与观察和治疗病人有关的，尤指在病床边而非在理论层面
senses.example: Clinical medicine begins with listening carefully to the patient.
senses.exampleCN: 临床医学从仔细倾听病人开始。
senses.why: Greek kline meant 'bed', and klinike techne was 'the practice at the sickbed'. Clinical marks whatever happens at that bed rather than in a lecture hall.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kline 意为“床”，klinike techne 是“病床边的实践”。clinical 标记的是发生在那张床边、而不是讲堂里的事。

senses.title: Clinic-based: belonging to an outpatient setting
senses.titleCN: 诊所的：属于门诊场所的
senses.definition: relating to a clinic or to outpatient care rather than a long hospital stay
senses.definitionCN: 与诊所或门诊护理有关，而非长期住院
senses.example: The hospital opened a clinical wing for outpatients last month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院上月启用了一个门诊临床区。
senses.why: Clinic shifted from 'bedridden person' to 'private hospital' in the 1880s. Clinical followed the building where beds are laid out, so the place gave its name to the service.
senses.whyCN: clinic 在 1880 年代从“卧床的人”转为“私立医院”。clinical 跟着那栋摆着病床的楼走，于是场所把名字给了服务。

senses.title: Observed signs: evidence the body shows
senses.titleCN: 临床体征：身体直接呈现的证据
senses.definition: of symptoms or signs, observed directly in the patient rather than produced in a laboratory
senses.definitionCN: （症状或体征）直接观察病人所得，而非实验室制造出的
senses.example: The diagnosis rests on clinical signs rather than on lab tests.
senses.exampleCN: 诊断依据的是临床体征，而不是实验室检查。
senses.why: What is clinical is what the bedside reveals. A clinical sign is evidence the body presents to the observer, before any machine turns it into numbers.
senses.whyCN: “临床的”就是病床边能看出来的。临床体征是身体直接呈现给观察者的证据，还没被机器变成数字。

senses.title: Trial stage: testing a treatment in patients
senses.titleCN: 临床阶段的：在病人身上试验疗法
senses.definition: of research, carried out with patients rather than with cells or animals
senses.definitionCN: （研究）在病人身上进行，而不是在细胞或动物身上
senses.example: The drug entered clinical trials last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药去年春天进入了临床试验。
senses.why: Research becomes clinical when it moves from the lab bench to beds occupied by patients. The setting names the stage: the bed is the test site.
senses.whyCN: 研究从实验台移到有病人的床，就叫临床。场所命名了阶段：病床就是试验场。

senses.title: Coldly dispassionate: a report without feeling
senses.titleCN: 冷静客观的：不带感情的报告
senses.definition: expressing facts in a detached way, as if describing a medical case
senses.definitionCN: 以超然的方式陈述事实，仿佛在描述一个病例
senses.example: She gave a clinical account of the accident, without a trace of anger.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷静客观地叙述了那场事故，没有一丝怒意。
senses.why: This sense is recorded from 1928: a doctor describes a body as a case, not as a person. Detachment is the tone of the bedside carried into ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 这一义记录于 1928 年：医生把身体描述为一个病例，而不是一个人。超然就是病床边的语调被带进了日常语言。

senses.title: Analytical: cutting straight to the measurable
senses.titleCN: 精准分析的：直接切到可量之处
senses.definition: precise and analytical, focusing on measurable detail and excluding emotion
senses.definitionCN: 精准而分析性的，聚焦可衡量的细节，排除情绪
senses.example: The coach took a clinical look at every mistake in the video.
senses.exampleCN: 教练冷静精准地看了录像里的每一个失误。
senses.why: From a medical report to any report: a clinical judgment strips away feeling and keeps only what can be counted or seen, as if the subject lay on an examination table.
senses.whyCN: 从病历报告扩展到任何报告：临床判断剥去情绪，只留下能数、能看见的东西，仿佛对象正躺在检查台上。

senses.title: Plain and functional: bare as an examination room
senses.titleCN: 简朴实用的：像检查室一样素净
senses.definition: plain, bare and functional in appearance, without decoration
senses.definitionCN: 外观素净、实用、没有装饰的
senses.example: The room was clinical: white walls, a metal bed and nothing else.
senses.exampleCN: 那房间很素净：白墙、一张铁床，别的什么都没有。
senses.why: A clinic is built for cleaning and examination, not for decoration. Bare white surfaces are what hygiene looks like, so anything similarly unadorned is called clinical.
senses.whyCN: 诊所是为清洁和检查而建，不为装饰。光裸的白色表面就是卫生的样子，于是任何同样无装饰的东西都被叫作 clinical。

senses.title: Bedside teaching: learning with real patients
senses.titleCN: 临床教学的：在真实病人身上学习
senses.definition: relating to the part of medical education carried out with real patients
senses.definitionCN: 与医学教育中面对真实病人的那部分有关
senses.example: Medical students spend their third year in clinical training.
senses.exampleCN: 医学生在第三年接受临床训练。
senses.why: The original Greek practice was instruction at the sickbed, with students watching the teacher examine a patient. Clinical names the half of learning that no textbook can supply.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原初的做法就是在病床边教学，学生看着老师检查病人。clinical 命名了教科书给不了的那一半学习。

senses.title: Diagnosable: a condition that earns the label
senses.titleCN: 临床诊断的：够得上这个标签的病症
senses.definition: of a condition, formally recognized and treated as an illness rather than a mood or habit
senses.definitionCN: （状况）被正式认定为疾病并加以治疗，而非仅是一时情绪或习惯
senses.example: The doctor treated it as clinical depression, not mere sadness.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把它当作临床抑郁症来治疗，而不只是悲伤。
senses.why: To call a condition clinical is to move it into the world of beds, charts and diagnostic criteria. It becomes an illness to be treated, not a mood to be endured.
senses.whyCN: 把一个状况叫作 clinical，就是把它移进病床、病历和诊断标准的世界。它成了要治疗的病，而不是要忍受的情绪。

intro.en: Clinical is the adjective of the sickbed. Greek kline 'bed' gave the word for a physician who visits patients in their beds, and English kept the bed in every later sense.
intro.cn: clinical 是病床的形容词。希腊语 kline“床”给出了“到床边看病人的医生”一词，英语在后来每个义项里都保留着那张床。

items.en: Kline meant 'bed, couch, that on which one lies'. From it came klinikos 'of the bed' and klinike techne 'the practice at the sickbed'.
items.cn: kline 意为“床、卧榻、人躺卧其上之物”。由它产生 klinikos“床的”和 klinike techne“病床边的实践”。

items.en: Latin clinicus meant 'a physician who visits patients in their beds', a direct borrowing of the Greek idea of medicine done at the bed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 clinicus 意为“到病人床边看病的医生”，直接借用了希腊语“在床边行医”的观念。

items.en: The noun clinic first meant 'a bedridden person, one confined to bed by sickness'. A related sense was 'one who defer baptism until the death-bed' (1660s).
items.cn: 名词 clinic 最初指“卧床的人、因病困在床上的人”。相关义项还有“拖延到临终才受洗的人”（1660 年代）。

items.en: Clinical is recorded in 1780 as 'pertaining to hospital patients or hospital care', formed from clinic + -al. The earlier adjective was clinic 'of the sick-bed' from the 1620s.
items.cn: clinical 记录于 1780 年，意为“与医院病人或医院护理有关的”，由 clinic + -al 构成。更早的形容词是 1620 年代的 clinic“病床的”。

items.en: Clinic 'private hospital' comes from German Klinik in 1884, through the notion of bedside teaching. Clinical 'coldly dispassionate' is recorded from 1928, like a medical report.
items.cn: clinic 的“私立医院”义来自 1884 年的德语 Klinik，经由“床边教学”的观念。clinical“冷静不带感情”记录于 1928 年，如一份病历报告。

items.en: Kline is traced to PIE *klei- 'to lean', also behind incline, decline and recline. The reconstructed root has no written attestation, so the deepest step is source uncertain.
items.cn: kline 被追溯到原始印欧语 *klei-“倾斜”，incline、decline、recline 也出自这里。该重构词根没有书面记录，故最深层来源不确定。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: a place where people receive medical advice or treatment. It is the noun that clinical was built on.
entries.definitionCN: 诊所；门诊部。它是 clinical 所依附的名词。

entries.definition: a doctor who treats patients directly rather than doing only research. It is clinic + -ian.
entries.definitionCN: 临床医生。它是 clinic 加 -ian，指直接看病人而非只做研究的医生。

entries.definition: to settle a matter or secure a win. It shares the clin- opening but is unrelated to beds.
entries.definitionCN: 敲定；确保获胜。它同样以 clin- 开头，但与病床无关。

entries.definition: to lean or slope, or to tend toward something. It comes from the same *klei- 'to lean' root as kline.
entries.definitionCN: 倾斜；倾向于。它与 kline 同出 *klei-“倾斜”词根。

entries.definition: relating to medicine in general. It is broader than clinical and can describe theory as well as practice.
entries.definitionCN: 医学的。它比 clinical 更宽，既可指实践也可指理论。

entries.definition: not showing personal feelings. It matches the 'coldly dispassionate' sense but says nothing about beds.
entries.definitionCN: 超然的；不带个人感情的。它对应“冷静客观”义，但不涉及病床。

entries.definition: based on facts rather than feelings. It is close to the analytical sense of clinical.
entries.definitionCN: 客观的；基于事实而非感情的。它接近 clinical 的分析义。

entries.definition: calm and not influenced by emotion. It is the direct synonym of clinical in its 1928 sense.
entries.definitionCN: 冷静公正的；不受情绪影响的。它就是 clinical 1928 年那一义的直接同义词。

entries.definition: free from bacteria, or lacking warmth and life. It overlaps with the plain, bare sense of clinical.
entries.definitionCN: 无菌的；也指缺乏生气。它与 clinical 的素净、无装饰义重叠。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Greek kline 'bed', the clinic family, and the derived forms English actually uses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：希腊语 kline“床”、clinic 词族，以及英语实际使用的派生形式。

normal.en: clinical = kline 'bed' + -al: whatever belongs to the sickbed.
normal.cn: clinical = kline“床”+ -al：属于病床的一切。

normal.en: clinic first meant a bedridden person, then the building where such people were treated.
normal.cn: clinic 先指卧床的人，再指治疗这些人的那栋楼。

normal.en: A clinical report sounds like a doctor reading a chart: facts only, no anger, no tears.
normal.cn: clinical 的报告听起来像医生读病历：只有事实，没有怒气，没有眼泪。

normal.en: A clinical trial is named for its setting: the trial happens at patients' beds, not at a lab bench.
normal.cn: 临床试验因场所得名：试验发生在病人床边，不在实验台。

normal.en: A clinical room is white, bare and easy to clean, because a clinic is built for hygiene rather than beauty.
normal.cn: clinical 的房间洁白、空旷、好打扫，因为诊所是为卫生而非美观而建。

abstract.en: The core operation is looking at a person the way a doctor looks at a case: closely, but from outside.
abstract.cn: 核心动作是像医生看病例那样看一个人：看得很近，但站在外面。

abstract.en: The bed supplies both the authority and the chill: nearness to suffering produces detachment as its professional tone.
abstract.cn: 病床同时提供权威与寒意：离痛苦太近，超然就成了它的职业语调。

abstract.en: So medical care, detached tone, precise analysis and bare surfaces are one stance: examine, measure, do not merge.
abstract.cn: 所以医疗服务、冷静语气、精准分析与素净表面是同一种姿态：检查、测量，但不与之融为一体。

examples.en: The new drug is still in clinical trials.
examples.cn: 这种新药仍在临床试验中。

examples.en: He described the scene in a clinical, almost cold voice.
examples.cn: 他用一种冷静、近乎冷淡的声音描述了那个场景。

examples.en: The ward was clean and clinical, with no flowers allowed.
examples.cn: 病房干净而素净，不允许摆放鲜花。

dict_mnemonic.text: cli 像 clean（干净）+ ni 像 nurse（护士）——干净得像护士站的病房 → clinical 临床的、冷静的

root: 源自希腊语 kline“床、卧榻”，经 klinikos“床的”、拉丁语 clinicus“床边行医的医生”进入英语，核心是“病床边”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of clinical, all traced to one place: the sickbed. What happens at the bed is medical; the tone used at the bed is detached; the room built for the bed is bare; and a condition serious enough for the bed is diagnosable.
sensesIntro.cn: clinical 的九个义项都追溯到一个地方：病床。床边发生的事是医疗；床边用的语气是冷静；为病床而建的房间是素净；严重到需要上床的状况是可诊断的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doctor at the sickbed, observing closely and recording without feeling.
core.cn: 核心意象：医生守在病床边，看得仔细，记录时不掺感情。

branches.en: THE BED DEFINES THE MEDICINE: care at the patient's bed, and the clinic building where that bed stands.
branches.cn: 病床定义了医学：病人床边的照护，以及摆放那张床的诊所大楼。

branches.en: THE BED DEFINES THE EVIDENCE: signs the body shows, and trials run on patients rather than cells.
branches.cn: 病床定义了证据：身体呈现的体征，以及在病人而非细胞身上做的试验。

branches.en: THE BED DEFINES THE TONE: a case described without feeling, and any judgment stripped to measurable detail.
branches.cn: 病床定义了语调：不带感情地描述病例，以及任何被剥到可量细节的判断。

branches.en: THE BED DEFINES THE ROOM: white, bare and easy to clean, because hygiene outranks decoration.
branches.cn: 病床定义了房间：洁白、空旷、易打扫，因为卫生优先于装饰。

branches.en: THE BED DEFINES LEARNING AND ILLNESS: students learn at real beds, and a condition serious enough for the bed becomes a diagnosis.
branches.cn: 病床定义了学习与疾病：学生在真实的床边学习，严重到需要卧床的状况成为诊断。

intro.en: Clinical is clinic + -al. Its family shows the Greek bed-root kline, the person suffix -ian, the negation prefix non-, and the size prefixes pre- and sub-.
intro.cn: clinical 是 clinic + -al。它的词族展示了希腊语“床”词根 kline、表人后缀 -ian、否定前缀 non-，以及表程度前缀 pre- 与 sub-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is clinicus 'bedside physician', from Greek klinikos 'of the bed' and kline 'bed'. English added -al, -ian, -ly and the medical prefixes pre-, sub- and non-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 clinicus“床边医生”，出自希腊语 klinikos“床的”和 kline“床”。英语加上 -al、-ian、-ly 以及医学前缀 pre-、sub-、non-。

items.meaning: relating to patients, or detached and plain
items.meaningCN: 临床的；冷静客观的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The clinical staff meet every morning at eight.
items.exampleCN: 临床人员每天早上八点开会。

items.structure: Greek klinike (techne), practice at the sickbed
items.meaning: a place for medical advice or treatment
items.meaningCN: 诊所；门诊部（原指病床边的医术）
items.example: She works at a clinic in the suburbs.
items.exampleCN: 她在郊区的一家诊所工作。

items.meaning: a doctor who treats patients directly
items.example: The clinician ordered another blood test.
items.exampleCN: 临床医生又开了一项血液检查。

items.meaning: in a clinical manner; in medical terms
items.meaningCN: 临床上；冷静客观地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The patient was clinically dead for two minutes.
items.exampleCN: 这名病人在临床上死亡了两分钟。

items.meaning: before a treatment is tested in patients
items.meaningCN: 临床前的；试验前的（pre- 表之前）
items.example: The drug passed preclinical tests on mice.
items.exampleCN: 这种药通过了在小鼠身上的临床前试验。

items.meaning: present but not strong enough to show clear symptoms
items.meaningCN: 亚临床的；症状不明显的（sub- 表低于）
items.example: The infection remained subclinical for weeks.
items.exampleCN: 感染在数周内一直处于亚临床状态。

items.meaning: not related to direct patient care
items.example: She moved from research into a nonclinical role.
items.exampleCN: 她从研究转到了非临床岗位。

items.meaning: a clinic treating many kinds of disease
items.meaningCN: 综合诊所；多科诊所（poly- 表多）
items.example: The polyclinic has cardiology and dermatology units.
items.exampleCN: 这家综合诊所有心脏科和皮肤科。

items.meaning: combining bedside findings with the study of disease tissue
items.meaningCN: 临床病理的（临床 + 连接元音 + 病理的）
items.example: The case was settled by clinicopathological review.
items.exampleCN: 这个病例通过临床病理复核得以定论。

latinEntries.meaning: a physician who visits patients in their beds
latinEntries.meaningCN: 到病人床边看病的医生
